FOLLOWING IS TEXT OF ARTICLE WHICH APPEARED IN IRAN TIMES ON SEPTEMBER 8: : SENATE PROBES SAVAK IN U.S. THE SENATE FOREIGN RELATIONS COMMITTEE IS INVESTIGATING A NUMBER OF U.S. CITIES PLAGUED BY IRANIAN STUDENT TURMOIL TO SEE IF SAVAK IS STIRRING UP THE TROUBLE, SENATE SOURCES TOLD THE IRAN TIMES. THE SUBCOMMITTEE ON INTERNATIONAL OPERATIONS, CHAIRED BY THE LIBERAL DEMOCRAT SENATOR GEORGE S. MCGOVERN, IS LOOKING INTO WHAT SAVAK IS DOING IN THIS COUNTRY, BUT NOT IRANIAN STUDENT ASSOCIATION FINANCING, THE SENATE SOURCES SAID. THE ISA WAS REPORTED TO HAVE SPENT DOLS 200,000 FOR A RECENT DEMONSTRATION IN WASHINGTON.

THE SENATE INTELLIGENCE COMMITEE IS ALSO REPORTEDLY LOOKING INTO SAVAK ACTIVITIES IN THE UNITED STATES. BUT THAT COMMITTEE OPERATES VERY QUIETLY AND RARELY REVEALS MUCH OF ITS WORK. THE SENATE SOURCES TOLD THE IRAN TIMES THAT THE MCGOVERN SUBCOMMITTEE IS "CONSIDERING HEARINGS ON SAVAK OPERATIONS WITHIN U.S. BORDERS. SUBCOMMITTEE INVESTIGATORS ARE KNOWN TO HAVE QUESTIONED OFFICIALS IN CHICO, CALIFORNIA, WHERE TWO IRANIAN STUDENTS WERE ACQUITTED IN JULY OF ATTEMPTING TO MURDER A POLITICAL FOE. THE TWO ACQUITTED, BEHDAD BAHMANOU AND ABOLFAZL GHAMSARI, HAD BEEN LABELLED SAVAK AGENTS BY THE CONFEDERATION OF IRANIAN STUDENTS.

THE VICTIM, ABDOLLAH MALEKOSHOARI, IS AN ANTI-SHAH ACTIVIST ATTENDING CHICO STATE UNIVERSITY. .EN KLASSEN, THE INVESTIGATOR WHO FRAMED THE CASE AGAINST THE ALLEGED PAIR OF SAVAK AGENTS,HE HAS NO SUCH INFORMATION. THE DEFENSE LAWYERS AND JUDGE IN THE CHICO TRIAL BOTH QUESTIONED WHETHER POLITICAL MOTIVES WERE BEHIND MALEKOSHOARI'S CHARGES THAT BAHMANOU AND GHAMSARI TRIED TO KILL HIM. DURING THE TRIAL, SUPERIOR COURT JUDGE LUCIAN B. VANDEGRIFT, TOLD PROSECUTOR LEO STEIDLMAYER TO CHECK IF HIS OFFICE WAS BEING "USED AND ABUSED" BY THE ANTISHAH WITNESSES FOR POLITICAL PURPOSES.

PROSECUTOR STEIDLMAYER TOLD THE CHICO ENTERPRISE-RECORD T STREMARK WAS,IRRESPONSIBLE, DARRELL STEVENS, ONE OF THE ATTORNEYS DEFENDING THE PAR OF ACCUSED SAVAK AGENTS, BELIEVES THE VICTIM, MALEK OSHOARI, PROVOKED THE SHOOTING, THEN SAW A CHANCE TO EMBARRASS A POLITICAL ADVERSARY BY PRESSING CHARGES. "REGARDLESS OF THE POLITICAL ANIMOSITY BACK AND FORTH," STEIDLMAYER SAID, "THIS INCIDENT (THE SHOOTING) DID HAPPEN" AND THE CASE HAD TO GO TO TRIAL FOR THE TRUTH TO COME OUT. DURING THE TRIAL NUMEROUS DEATH THREATS WERE MADE ON THE DEFENDANTS AND EXTRA SECURITY WAS REQUIRED. PROSECUTOR STEIDLMAYER SAID THE HEAVY SECURITY COSTS COULD LEAD HIS OFFICE TO DROP OTHER PROSECUTIONS INVOLVING IRANIANS.

STEIDLMAYER SAID HE AND DISTRICT ATTORNEY KEN LEACH ARE "CONSIDERING THE POSSIBILITIES" OF FILING PERJURY CHARGES AGAINST SOME OF THE ANTI-SHAH WITNESSES, BUT "IT'S A QUESTION OF HOW MUCH OF THE TAXPAYER' MONEY THE DEFENSE TEAM OF THREE LAWYERS AND TEN OTHERS WOLD NOT SAY HOW MUCH THEY CHARGED FOR THEIR WORK. BAHMANOU 'S LAWYER, STEVENS, SAID HE WAS BEING PAID BY HIS CLIENT WHOSE FATHER WAS A WEALTHY LAWYER IN IRAN. STEVENS SAID THE MONEY WAS NOT COMING FROM THE IRANIAN GOVERNMENT, AS SOME MEMBERS OF THE IRANIAN STUDENTS ASSOCIATION WHO DEMONSTRATED AT THE TRIAL HAVE CHARGED.
WE ARE SENDING COPY OF NEW YORK MAGAZINE ARTICLE TO EMBASSY VIA SPECIAL MESSENGER. CHRISTOPHER

MESSAGE IS CONSIDERED CONFIDENTIAL AND NO RELEASE IS PLANNED. EMBOFF ALSO SAID BRITS PLAN TO RELEASE SOME "POLICE EQUIPMENT" FOR IRAN. HE SAID IT WAS NOT CLEAR WHETHER DISTINCTION WAS MADE BETWEEN LETHAL AND NON-LETHAL ITEMS. WE TOLD HIM WE HAD RECENTLY RELEASED TEAR GAS AND OTHER NON-LETHAL EQUIPMENT, BUT HAD HELD IN SUSPENSE IRANIAN REQUESTS FOR GUNS.

FOR PARIS AND BONN. WOULD APPRECIATE ANY INFORMATION YOU HAVE ON SHOW OF SUPPORT FOR GOI BY HOST GOVERNMENT. 1978STATE233140.subject: REQUEST FOR APPROVAL OF EMPLOYMENT ACCEPTANCE BY DEPENDENT OF EMBOFF (DENNIS MENDYK)

segments.text: DEPT. CAN APPROVE ACCEPTANCE OF EITHER JOB OPPORTUNITY DESCRIBED REF B.
DEPT. DOES NOT APPROVE RENEWED REQUEST FOR AUTHORIZATION TO POST TO APPROVE "WAIVERS OF IMMUNITY".

DEPT. CONCERNED OVER POST'S IRE RELATING TO ACTION ON REQUESTS FOR APPROVAL OF EMPLOYMENT OFFERS. NEARLY ONE MONTH IS INDEED A LONG TIME IN WHICH TO ANSWER A CABLE, ALBEIT ONE NOT FLAGGED WITH ANY URGENCY. NEVERTHELESS, HUMAN RESOURCES ARE AT PLAY AT BOTH THE SENDING AND RECEIVING ENDS. IT IS NOT, FOR EXAMPLE, POSSIBLE FOR DEPT. TO ASCERTAIN THE FRAGILITY OF JOB OFFERS IN QUESTION IF CABLE RECEIVED IN ROUTINE FASHION WITH NO MENTION OF THE SAME.

IT IS ALSO TRUE THAT AUGUST IS A POPULAR MONTH FOR VACATIONS, AND IT IS NOT UNHEARD OF, CERTAINLY NOT UNUSUAL ON THIS END FOR A ROUTINE MATTER TO BE "HELD" FOR THE ACTION OFFICER UNTIL HIS RETURN FROM AN OFTEN MUCH-NEEDED RESPITE FROM OTHER ROUTINE OR NOT-SO-ROUTINE RESPONSIBILITIES.

POST IS ALSO REMINDED THAT WHEN A CABLE IS RECEIVED IN THIS COMPUTERIZED DEPT., THERE ARE ANY NUMBER OF "ACTION" DESTINATIONS WHERE IT MAY LAND. IN THE CASE OF THE REFERENCED MESSAGES FROM POST, ACTION INDEED HAD TO BE TRANSFERRED AND, IN THE PROCESS, GOT CAUGHT UP IN VACATION SCHEDULES, AS WELL AS AN INNOCENT OMISSION ON THE PART OF THE SENDING OFFICE TO NOTIFY THE RECEIVING OFFICE THAT THE MATTER WAS TRULY "URGENT".

IN ORDER TO AVOID FUTURE MISUNDERSTANDINGS, PARTICULARLY RELATING TO QUESTIONING OF THE DEPT.'S COMMITMENT TO GIVE EXPEDITED TREATMENT TO THE REQUESTS IN QUESTION, CAN NOT THE EMBASSY GIVE A CLEARER INDICATION IN THE INITIAL MESSAGE OF THE TIME FRAME AND, HENCE, "URGENCY" OF THE EMPLOYMENT OFFER AND LABEL THE TELEGRAM ACCORDINGLY? IN ADDITION, DEPT. WOULD SUGGEST THAT POST ADDRESS MESSAGES TO THE ATTENTION OF L/M AND NEA/EX, AS REQUIRED IN THE REGULATIONS. IN THAT WAY, AT LEAST TWO OFFICES WOULD RECEIVE A PIECE OF THE "ACTION" AND, PERHAPS, SLIPPAGE THROUGH THE DEPT.'S CRACKS CAN BE MINIMIZED. CHRISTOPHER

LANGUAGE COMPARISON BETWEEN ENGLISH AND PERSIAN TEXTS OF THE AGREEMENT FOR COOPERATION BETWEEN U.S. AND IRAN CONCERNING PEACEFUL USES OF NUCLEAR ENERGY HAS BEEN COMPLETED. WE HAVE REVIEWED DISCREPANCIES INDICATED BY LANGUAGE COMPARISON AND HAVE DECIDED THAT THOSE INDICATED BELOW SHOULD BE RAISED WITH IRANIANS IN ORDER TO INSURE COMPLETE CONCORDANCE BETWEEN ENGLISH AND PERSIAN TEXTS. AT THIS POINT, ENGLISH TEXT IS ONLY ONE INITIALED, AND EVERY EFFORT MUST BE MADE TO INSURE THAT PERSIAN TEXT COMPLETELY AND ACCURATELY REFLECTS ENGLISH TEXT. YOU SHOULD POINT OUT, IN DISCUSSION WITH IRANIANS, THAT USG LANGUAGE COMPARISON INDICATES FOLLOWING PROBLEMS, AND YOU SHOULD SEEK APPROPRIATE MODIFICATION OF PERSIAN TEXT.

MODIFICATIONS SHOULD BE CABLED TO DEPARTMENT IN TRANSLITERATED FORM SO THAT LANGUAGE SERVICES MAY CHECK. IF IRANIANS DO NOT WISH TO MAKE ANY OF REQUESTED CHANGES, PLEASE SEEK EXPLANATION AND REPORT TO DEPARTMENT ASAP. REQUESTED CHANGES ARE KEYED TO INITIALED VERSION OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEXT OF AGREEMENT AND NOTE.

PAGE 3, ARTICLE 2 (C), LINES 4-5: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "..., OR ANY OTHER ITEM SO DESIGNATED...." PERSIAN TEXT (TRANSLATED INTO ENGLISH) READS: "..., OR ANY OTHER FACILITY SO DESIGNATED...., SINCE WORDS "ITEM" AND FACILITY" ARE USED IN DIFFERENT SENSE IN AGREEMENT, WITH FORMER INCLUDING COMPONENTS OF FACILITIES, WE REQUEST IRANIAN CHANGE PERSIAN TEXT TO CONFORM TO ENGLISH TEXT.

PAGE 4, ARTICLE 2 (K), LINES 3-5: ENGLISH TEXT STATES: "...BUT DO NOT INCLUDE USE IN, RESEARCH ON OR DEVELOPMENT OF ANY NUCLEAR EXPLOSIVE DEVICE, OR...., PERSIAN TEXT STATES: ,BUT DO NOT INCLUDE RESEARCH ON USE OR PRODUCTION OF NUCLEAR EXPLOSIVE DEVICES, OR...., "DEVELOPMENT" HAS BEEN OMITTED FROM THE PERSIAN TEXT, AND WE REQUEST THAT IT BE INCLUDED. WE NOTE THAT THE P:RSIAN TRANSLATION OF ARTICLE 8 USES TERM "DEVELOPMENT, AND WE BELIEV- ARTICLE 2 (K) AND 8 SHOULD BE CONSISTENT IN THIS RESPECT.

PAGE 5, ARTICLE 2 (T), LINE 1: THE :NGLISH TEXT STATES: 'UTILIZATION FACILITY' MEANS ANY REACTOR OTHER THAN ONE DESIGNED OR...., THE PERSIAN TEXT STATES: "'UTILIZATION FACILITY' MEANS ANY REACTOR DESIGNED OR...." THUS THPERSIAN TEXT IS EXACTLY OPPOSITE OF ENGLISH TEXT, SINCE IT DOES NOT CONTAIN WORDS "OTHER THAN ONE". THESE WORDS SHOULD BE INSERTED.

PAGE 6, ARTICLE 4(1), LINE ;: THE ENGLISH TEXT READS: "HOWEVER, SENSITIVE NUCL:AR FACILITIES AND MAJOR CRITICAL COMPONENTS...., THE PERSIAN TEXT READS: "HOWEVER, SENSITIVE NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY AND BASIC SENSITIVE COMPONENTS...." FIRST, WE POINT OUT THAT SENSITIVE NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY IS DEALT WITH IN ARTICLE 3(4). IT IS A DEFINED T:RM. IT IS INAPPROPRIATE TO USE "SEHSITIVE NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY" IN ARTICLE 4(1) WHICH REFERS TO TRANSFER OF MATERIAL, EQUIPMENT AND COMPONENTS, AND NOT RPT NOT TECHNOLOGY OR INFORMATION. TERM "SENSITIVE NUCLEAR FA-ILITIES, SHOULD BE USED INSTEAD, AS IN ENGLISH TEXT. THIS TERM IS DEFINED IN ARTICLE 2 (P).

WITH RESPECT TO USE OF TERM "BASIC SENSITIVE COMPONENTS" AS OPPOS:D TO "MAJOR CRITICAL COMPONENTS,, ,MAJOR CRITICAL COMPONENT" IS TERM D-FINED IN ARTICLE 2 (F) AND SHOULD BE USED THROUGHOUT AGREEMENT.

PAGE 7, ARTICLE 4(2), LINE 13: ENGLISH TEXT STATES: "...TO BE TRANSFERRED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT...., PERSIAN TEXT STATES: ,TO BE TRANSFERRED TO IRAN UNDER THIS AGREEMENT...." FROM ENGLISH CONTEXT, IT IS CLEAR THAT SENTENCE INVOLVES ONLY TRANSFERS TO IRAN. IF IT IS NECESSARY GRAMMATICALLY TO INCLUDE "TO IRAN" IN PERSIAN TEXT, WE WOULD BE PREPARED TO CONFORM ENGLISH TEXT BY ALSO INCLUDING THIS REFERENCE. WE WISH TO KEEP TEXTS IDENTICAL.

PAGE 9, ARTICLE 5 (1), LINE 6: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "...OR HIGH ENRICHED URANIUM,...." PERSIAN TEXT READS: "...OR THE PRODUCED HIGH ENRICHED URANIUM...., INSERTION OF THE PRODUCED, IN PERSIAN CHANGES MEANING, AND WE REQUEST TEXT BE CONFORMED TO ENGLIS; TEXT.

PAGE 11, ARTICLE 8, LINE 6: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "...FOR RESEARCH ON OR DEVELOPMENT OF ANY NUCLEAR...." PERSIAN TEXT READS: "...FOR RESEARCH ON AND DEVELOPMENT OF NUCLEAR...." PERSIAN TEXT HAS SUBSTITUTED WORD "AND" FOR WORD "OR". THIS CHANGES MEANING, AND IS INCONSISTENT WITH FORMAT USED IN ARTICLE 2 (K). WORD "AND" SHOULD BE REPLACED BY WORD "OR". IN ADDITION, WORD "ANY" WHICH HAS BEEN DELETED SHOULD BE INSERTED.

PAGE 14, ARTICLE 10, TITLE: ENGLISH TEXT READS: ,MULTIPLE SUPPLIER CONTROLS". PERSIAN TEXT READS: "MULTIPLE SUPPLIERS CONTROL,. THUS, "SUPPLIER" IS SINGULAR IN ENGLISH AND PLURAL IN PERSIAN, WHILE ,CONTROL" IS PLURAL IN ENGLISH AND SINGULAR IN PERSIAN. WE WOULD PREFER TEXTS BE IDENTICAL, HAVE SLIGHT PREFERENC: FOR ENGLISH VERSION, BUT W: ARE WILLING TO ADOPT WHICHEVER FORMAT IRANIANS PREFER, AND CONFORM TEXTS APPROPRIATELY.

PAGE 17, ARTICLE 14(1), LINE 3: ENGLISH TEXT READS: ,...WITH THEIR APPLICABLE REQUIREMENTS...., PERSIAN TEXT READS: "...WITH THEIR CURRENT REQUIREMENTS...." TERM ,CURRENT, IS DIFFERENT FROM ,APPLICABLE,, AND WE BELIEVE ,APPLICABLE" IS THE APPROPRIATE WORD.

ANNEX, CATEGORY I, LINE 5: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "...TO PERSONS WHOSE TRUSTWORTHINESS HAS BEEN DETERMINED...." PERSIAN TEXT READS: ,TO TRUSTWORTHY PERSONS...." ENGLISH TEXT CONVEYS NUANCE THAT SEPARATE DETERMINATION MUST BE MADE REGARDING TRUSTWORTHINESS, BRINGING TO MIND SOME SORT OF CLEARANC: PROCEDURE. PERSIAN TEXT, ON OTHER HAND, HAS AIR OF INFORMALITY AND DOES NOT SPECIFY NEED FOR PARTICULAR DETERMINATION. THUS, WE PREFER ENGLISH VERSION, AND WOULD REQUEST PERSIAN TEXT BE CONFORMED.

PAGE 3 OF NOTE, PARA 2, LINES 3-4: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "...ARRANGEMENTS FOR SUBSEQUENT DISPOSITION OF IRRADIATED...." PERSIAN TEXT READS: "...FOR SUBSEQUENT ARRANGEMENTS OF IRRADIATED...." WE DO NOT BELIEVE PERSIAN VERSION IS EASILY UNDERSTOOD, OR CONVEYS SAME SENSE AS ENGLISH VERSION. WE THINK IT IMPORTANT THAT REFERENCE BE MADE TO SUBSEQUENT ,DISPOSITION". THUS, PERSIAN TEXT SHOULD B: CONFORMED TO ENGLISH TEXT.

PAGE ; OF NOTE, ITEM C, LINE 1: ENGLISH TEXT READS: ,...STORAGE, PROCESSING OR OTHER DISPOSITION...." PERSIAN TEXT READS: "STORAGE, RECYCLING OR OTHER ACTIONS...." FIRST, TRANSLATION OF WORD "PROCESSING" AS ,RECYCLING" IS INACCURATE. SINCE PERSIAN TEXT TRANSLATES "PROCESSING" AS "REPROCESSING, IN ITEM B, LINES 3-4 ON PAG: 3 OF NOTE, WE BELIEVE IT APPROPRIATE THAT "PROCESSING, IN ITEM C BE TRANSLATED IN IDENTICAL FASHION, I.E., AS "REPROCESSING." HOWEVER, IF FEASIBLE IN PERSIAN LANGUAGE, WE WOULD PREFER THAT PERSIAN TEXT USE WORD "PROCESSING" IN BOTH ITEMS B AND C (AND OTHER PLACES WORD "PROCESSING" APPEARS IN ENGLISH TEXT).
SECOND, WE DO NOT BELIEVE WORD "ACTIONS" APPROPRIATELY CONVEYS SENSE OF "DISPOSITION", AND BELIEVE ENGLISH TEXT SHOULD BE FOLLOWED IN PERSIAN VERSION AS WELL.

PAGE 4 OF NOTE, ITEM C, LINE 1: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "PROLIFERATION...." PERSIAN TEXT READS: "...NUCLEAR ARMS PROLIFERATION...., WE REQUEST DELETION OF WORDS "NUCLEAR ARMS" FROM PERSIAN TEXT, AS THIS LANGUAGE IS NOT CONTAINED IN ENGLISH TEXT. (FYI: USE OF "NUCLEAR ARMS" INSERTS POSSIBILITY OF ARGUING DISTINCTION BETWEEN WEAPONS AND PNES. END FYI)

PAGE 4 OF NOTE, LINE 17: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "..., WITH DISPOSITION OF...." PERSIAN TEXT READS: "...AND APPLICATION OF...., WE DO NOT BELIEVE TERM "APPLICATION" APPROPRIATELY REFLECTS MEANING OF TERM "DISPOSITION", AND REQUEST PERSIAN TEXT BE MODIFIED TO REFLECT ENGLISH TEXT.

PAGE 4 OF NOTE, LINE 20: ENGLISH TEXT READS: ,WITH SPECIFIC REFERENCE TO...., PERSIAN TEXT READS: "WITH REFERENCE TO...., WHILE WE PREFER INCLUSION OF WORD "SPECIFIC", WE COULD ACCEPT ITS DELETION IF IRANIANS PREFER. WE BELIEVE ENGLISH AND PERSIAN TEXTS SHOULD BE IDENTICAL, AND THUS WOULD LIKE TO KNOW GOI PREFERENCE.

PAGE 5 OF NOTE, LINE 1: ENGLISH TEXT READS: "...IRAN WITH BENEFITS COMPARABLE...., PERSIAN TEXT READS: "...IRAN WITH RESOURCES COMPARABLE...." DEPARTMENT LANGUAGE SERVICES BELIEVES PERSIAN TEXT REFLECTS TYPOGRAPHICAL ERROR. WORD ,BENEFITS" IN PERSIAN IS ,MANAFE'" WHICH IS VERY SIMILAR TO THE WORD ,MANABE'", MEANING "RESOURCES;. PLEASE INSURE THAT TYPOGRAPHICAL ERROR IS CORRECTED. IF THIS IS NOT A TYPOGRAPHICAL ERROR, DEPT STILL CONSIDERS WORD "BENEFITS" TO B: THE CORRECT TERM WHICH SHOULD BE USED IN PERSIAN TEXT.

AS MATTER SEPARATE FROM QUESTIONS RAISED BY LANGUAGE COMPARISON, IN INFORMAL CONSULTATIONS WITH CONGRESSIONAL STAFFERS ON AGREEMENT, TWO MINOR CLARIFICATIONS IN ENGLISH TEST OF NOTE HAVE BEEN SUGGESTED. WE BELIEVE MAKING THESE CHANGES WOULD HELP US ENLIST SUPPORT OF KEY STAFFERS, AND THUS IMPROVE OUR POSITION IN HILL CONSIDERATION OF AGREEMENT. REASON: SENTENCE IS ALMOST DIRECT FROM FIRST SENTENCE OF SECTION 101 OF NON-PROLIFERATION ACT EXCEPT FOR ABOVE CLAUSE. PROPOSED MODIFICATION WOULD MAKE SENTENCE CONFORM AND ELIMINATE ANY CONCERN AS TO WHY LANGUAGE CHANGED OR ABOUT DISTINCTIONS BETWEEN "OBJECTIVES" AND "POLICIES". (B) PAGE 3 OF NOTE, ITEM C, LINES 3-4: INSERT AFTER "THIS ALTERNATIVE WOULD INCLUDE" THE PHRASE "AS AN OPTION". REASON: OBVIOUSLY, SECOND SENTENCE IN ITEM C ONLY REFERS TO PROCESSING ALTERNATIVE. HOWEVER, THE WORDS "WOULD INCLUDE" MIGHT BE READ AS INDICATIVE THAT THE SECOND SENTENCE APPLIED TO STORAGE OR OTHER DISPOSITION.
WE WOULD LIKE TO CLEAR UP THIS AMBIGUITY TO PREVENT THE ARGUMENT THAT ANY COURSE OF ACTION UNDER ITEM C NECESSARILY MUST INCLUDE PROCESSING IN THE UK OR FRANCE. CHRISTOPHER

1978STATE234445.subject: ZAHEDI CALL ON ACTING SECRETARY SUMMARY: AMBASSADOR ZAHEDI GAVE ACTING SECRETARY FULL DESCRIPTION OF RECENT EVENTS IN IRAN FROM HIS PERS

segments.text: SUMMARY: AMBASSADOR ZAHEDI GAVE ACTING SECRETARY FULL DESCRIPTION OF RECENT EVENTS IN IRAN FROM HIS PERSPECTIVE. ACTING SECRETARY EMPHASIZED OUR SUPPORT FOR CONTINUING ECONOMIC REFORMS, POLITICAL LIBERALIZATION AND OUR HOPE THAT STIFF MEASURES (ARRESTS OF OPPOSITIONISTS AND JOURNALISTS) WERE ONLY TEMPORARY. HE SUGGESTED CLEAR STATEMENT TO THIS EFFECT WOULD BE REASSURING TO IRAN'S FRIENDS.
ACTING SECRETARY ASKED AMBASSADOR ZAHEDI TO COME IN SEPTEMBER 13 FOR A REVIEW OF SITUATION IN IRAN. MEETING LASTED ONE HOUR.

ACTING SECRETARY OPENED MEETING BY EMPHASIZING STRONG FEELINGS THAT AMERICANS HAVE FOR IRAN AS EXEMPLIFIED BY PRESIDENT'S MESSAGE TO THE SHAH AND RECENT FAVORABLE PRESS ARTICLES. ACTING SECRETARY NOTED AMBASSADOR'S RECENT RETURN FROM IRAN AND ASKED FOR HIS IMPRESSIONS OF LOCAL SCENE AND ASSESSMENT OF FUTURE PROSPECTS.
SUMMARY OF VERY LONG PRESENTATION BY ZAHEDI FOLLOWS

SHAH WAS TOTALLY COMMITTED TO BUILDING A STRONG AND ASSOCIATES. HOVEYDA IN PARTICULAR HAD LIED TO HIM ABOUT ACTUAL CONDITIONS IN THE COUNTRY AND LED SHAH TO BELIEVE THAT INSTITUTIONS WERE GENUINE WHEN THEY WERE IN EFFECT ONLY PAPER.

ZAHEDI HAD WORKED HARD TO DISABUSE IRANIAN LEADERS OF FICTION THAT US WAS SEEKING TO OVERTHROW THE SHAH. FORMER AND PRESENT PRIME MINISTERS SEEMED CONVINCED THAT US WAS BACKING OPPOSITION. AMOUZEGAR BELIEVED US AND USSR WERE PLANNING TO DIVIDE BETWEEN THEM WORLD'S ENERGY SOURCES WITH RUSSIANS TAKING IRAN AND US GETTING SAUDI ARABIA. ZAHEDI HAD MET WITH ALI AMINI AND OTHER OPPOSITION LEADERS WHO ALSO SEEMED TO BELIEVE US WAS BACKING THEM.

ZAHEDI HAD TOLD SHAH THAT HE FACED MANY PROBLEMS, INCLUDING INATTENTION TO RELIGIOUS GROUPS, COMMUNIST UNHAPPINESS WITH PROGRESS AND CLOSE US-IRAN TIES, SUPPLY OF OIL TO ISRAEL, CORRUPTION, LACK OF NEW FACES IN GOVERNMENT.

ZAHEDI TOLD SHAH THAT HE MUST GET RID OF HOVEYDA AND SOMEHOW BRING AN END TO CRITICISM OF THE ROYAL FAMILY. HE TOLD THE SHAH THAT PRINCESS ASHRAF SHOULD NOT GO TO UNGA THIS YEAR AND THAT OTHER MEMBERS OF THE ROYAL FAMILY (E.G. SHAMS AND MAHMOUD REZA) SHOULD LEAVE IRAN. GOI SHOULD PRESS ON WITH FREEDOM OF RELIGION, LAND DISTRIBUTION AND WOMEN'S RIGHTS.

WHEN HE SAW EXTENT OF ORGANIZATION OF DEMONSTRATIONS LAST WEEK, ZAHEDI WAS CONVINCED THAT NEW FACTOR, I.E. COMMUNIST LEADERSHIP, WAS PRESENT IN OPPOSITION. HE WAS ALSO SHOCKED BY IRRESPONSIBILITY OF PRESS WHEN CENSORSHIP LIFTED. ADDITIONALLY, MOBS THREATENED TO SPLIT ARMED FORCES AND OCCUPY GOVERNMENT MINISTRIES; MARTIAL LAW WAS NECESSARY TO PREVENT VERY SERIOUS VIOLENCE.

AS TO FUTURE, GOI HAD TO SHOW IT WAS NOT JOKING ON POLITICAL LIBERALIZATION AND THEREFORE PARLIAMENT DEBATES WERE BEING FULLY REPORTED ON RADIO AND TV. MARTIAL LAW WAS IMPOSED FOR SIX MONTHS BUT RESTRICTIONS WOULD BE PROGRESSIVELY LIGHTENED DURING THAT PERIOD.

MILITARY OFFICERS HAD TOLD HIM THAT YOUNGER OFFICERS WERE VERY UNHAPPY. SOME YOUNGER OFFICERS HAD TOLD ZAHEDI THEY WERE THINKING OF PLANNING A COUP BECAUSE THEY HAD BEEN "DISHONORED" BY GOVERNMENT'S FAILURE TO EXERCISE AUTHORITY.

FINALLY, ZAHEDI SAID THAT MARTIAL LAW WAS A SALUTARY SHOCK FOR THE SHAH. IT BROUGHT HOME TO HIM THAT EXTENSIVE REFORMS WERE NECESSARY. ZAHEDI WAS CONVINCED SHAH WOULD PERSIST WITH PROGRAM OF POLITICAL LIBERALIZATION.
ACTING SECRETARY MADE FOLLOWING POINTS WHICH WERE NOTED IN WRITING BY ZAHEDI

WE WERE GLAD ZAHEDI HAD COUNTERED RUMOR THAT US WAS INVOLVED IN IRANIAN INTERNAL AFFAIRS. THAT STORY WAS TOTALLY WITHOUT FOUNDATION. ACTING SECRETARY OFFERED HIS PERSONAL ASSURANCES THAT US WAS NOT INVOLVED IN ANY RESPECT IN IRANIAN POLITICS.

WE DEEMED IT IMPORTANT THAT IRAN CONTINUE WITH PROGRAM OF ECONOMIC REFORMS PROMISED BY THE SHAH. SUCH REFORMS ARE ESSENTIAL TO FUTURE HEALTH OF IRAN AND WE WERE GLAD THAT AMBASSADOR ZAHEDI WAS PUSHING THEM.
WE THOUGHT IT EQUALLY IMPORTANT THAT SHAH'S PROGRAM OF POLITICAL LIBERALIZATION CONTINUE.

WHILE IRAN'S FRIENDS UNDERSTOOD THE NEED TO RESTORE ORDER, IT IS IMPORTANT THAT MEASURES SUCH AS THOSE RECENTLY TAKEN BE ONLY TEMPORARY. IT WOULD BE VERY HELPFUL AND REASSURING TO IRAN'S FRIENDS IF A CLEAR STATEMENT TO THIS EFFECT COULD BE ISSUED IN TEHRAN. ZAHEDI WAS FAMILIAR WITH US REACTION TO SUCH EVENTS.

COMMENTING ON LAST POINT ZAHEDI SAID HE WAS CONFIDENT THAT MARTIAL LAW MEASURES WERE ONLY TEMPORARY. HE WAS TOLD ONLY 12 TO 15 OPPOSITION PERSONALITIES HAD BEEN ARRESTED. HE ACKNOWLEDGED THAT IN PRESENT CONFUSED CIRCUMSTANCES SOME OF THOSE PICKED UP MIGHT BE INNOCENT OF ALL CHARGES.

IN CONCLUSION, ACTING SECRETARY SAID IT WAS IMPORTANT THAT WE STAY IN TOUCH, AND AS FRIENDS CONTINUE TO DRAW STRENGTH FROM EACH OTHER. AMBASSADOR ZAHEDI AGREED AND NOTED THAT HE WOULD BE SEEKING APPOINTMENT WITH THE SECRETARY AND MIGHT RETURN TO IRAN WITHIN A FEW DAYS TO SPEAK TO THE SHAH. HE OBSERVED THAT IRAN'S TROUBLES STEMMED IN PART FROM FACT THAT IT WAS SUCH A STAUNCH FRIEND OF THE US AND HAD CONSEQUENTLY ANGERED USSR. CHRISTOPHER

AT IRANIAN EMBASSY DINNER SEPTEMBER 19, EMBOFF (KAZEMIAN) APPROACHED DEPTOFF RE CHICAGO GRAND JURY INQUIRY, NOTING INVESTIGATION SEEMED TO BE STEPPED UP DURING THE PAST TWO WEEKS. EMBOFF HAD IN APRIL MENTIONED THAT HE MIGHT WISH TO DISCUSS INQUIRY WITH DEPTOFF, BUT HAD NOT FOLLOWED THROUGH BECAUSE HE THOUGHT FBI INTEREST HAD FADED. NOW, HE SAID, INVESTIGATION SEEMED HEADED IN VERY DELICATE DIRECTION WITH OBJECT OF TRACING FUNDING OF PRO-SHAH DEMONSTRATORS. HE COULD NOT OVER-EMPHASIZE IMPORTANCE OF THIS ISSUE FOR US-IRANIAN RELATIONS.

SO FAR, EMBOFF SAID, INVESTIGATION DID NOT TOUCH EMBASSY AND CONCERNED ONLY CONSULATES, ESPECIALLY CHICAGO AND SAN FRANCISCO. HEADS OF BANK SADERAT IN SAN FRANCISCO AND BANK MELLI IN NEW YORK HAD BEEN CALLED TO TESTIFY. LAWYER FOR PRO-SHAH DEMONSTRATORS ALSO CALLED. IRANIAN REACTION TO INVESTIGATION WOULD BE HELPED SOMEWHAT IF IT ALSO TRUE THAT FBI WAS LOOKING INTO ANTI-SHAH DEMONSTRATIONS. DEPTOFF SAID HE HAD IMPRESSION THAT WAS THE CASE, BUT THAT INQUIRY HAD NOT YET PRODUCED USEFUL EVIDENCE.

EMBOFF REFERRED TO NEW YORK MAGAZINE ARTICLE ON SAVAK AND SAID EMBASSY'S US LAWYER HAD CALLED ON SENIOR DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE OFFICIAL REGARDING POSSIBLE LEGAL ACTIONS. DEPTOFF OBSERVED THAT ARTICLE WAS SENSATIONAL PIECE WHICH CONTAINED NUMBER OF OBVIOUS INACCURACIES. TO DATE IT HAD PRODUCED VIRTUALLY NO QUESTIONS EITHER FROM PRESS OR CONGRESS. IN FACT, ONLY ONE PAPER HAD CALLED IRANIAN DESK TO ASK ABOUT ACCURACY OF TWO STATEMENTS IN ARTICLE ATTRIBUTED TO STATE DEPARTMENT. DESK HAD DENIED DEPARTMENT SPOKESMAN MADE SUCH STATEMENTS.

IN CONCLUSION, EMBOFF SAID THAT APPEARANCE OF ARTICLE AND INTENSIFIED INVESTIGATION WERE VERY UNFORTUNATE. HE HAD LONG EXPERIENCE IN US AND UNDERSTOOD WORKINGS OF AMERICAN PRESS AND GOVERNMENT. BUT OTHER IRANIANS, CYNICAL AND LACKING THIS KNOWLEDGE, WERE CONVINCED THAT EXECUTIVE BRANCH HAD INSPIRED ARTICLE AND WAS PUSHING INVESTIGATION AGAINST GOI AS PART OF POLITICAL GAME US WAS PLAYING

1978STATE239863.subject: MESSAGE FROM THE SHAH IRANIAN EMBASSY HAS TRANSMITTED TO THE WHITE HOUSE FOLLOW- ING MESSAGE FROM THE SHAH

segments.text: IRANIAN EMBASSY HAS TRANSMITTED TO THE WHITE HOUSE FOLLOWING MESSAGE FROM THE SHAH: "DEAR MR. PRESIDENT, I THANK YOU FOR YOUR MESSAGE OF 18TH SEPTEMBER, THE CONTENTS OF WHICH I HAVE NOTED WITH GREAT INTEREST. I GREATLY APPRECIATE THE FACT THAT YOU HAVE INFORMED ME OF THE DETAILS OF THE HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT RESULTS ACHIEVED AT THE CAMP DAVID SUMMIT MEETING. THESE NO DOUBT CONSTITUTE AN HISTORICAL STEP AND A MAJOR BREAKTHROUGH IN THE SEARCH FOR PEACE IN THE MIDDLE EAST. IN THIS REGARD, I AM FULLY AWARE OF THE DECISIVE ROLE WHICH YOU HAVE PERSONALLY PLAYED, MR. PRESIDENT, IN THE VITAL PEACEMAKING PROCESS.

THE QUALITIES OF STATESMANSHIP, THE BREADTH OF VISION WHICH YOU HAVE DISPLAYED AND YOUR FIRM DEDICATION TO THE CAUSE OF WORLD PEACE AND SECURITY HAVE CONTRIBUTED IN AN OUTSTANDING MANNER TO THE SUCCESS OF THE MEETING. WHILST CONGRATULATING YOU MOST HEARTILY, MR. PRESIDENT, I SINCERELY HOPE THAT THE FRAMEWORK FOR THE RESOLUTION OF THE MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT AND YOUR UNTIRING EFFORTS IN THIS CONNECTION WHICH DESERVE GREAT ADMIRATION WILL PAVE THE WAY FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A JUST AND LASTING PEACE IN THE AREA. WITH MY KINDEST REGARDS. SINCERELY, MOHAMMAD REZA PAHLAVI". CHRISTOPHER

1978STATE242478.subject: NAMIBIA: SOUTH AFRICA'S DECISION' FOLLOWING IS THE TEXT OF SOUTH AFRICAN'S REPLY TO THE AIDE MEMOIRE OF 16 SEPTEMBER 1978 FROM THE FIVE

segments.text: FOLLOWING IS THE TEXT OF SOUTH AFRICAN'S REPLY TO THE AIDE MEMOIRE OF 16 SEPTEMBER 1978 FROM THE FIVE WESTERN MEMBERS OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL: BEGIN TEXT

CESSATION OF VIOLENCE IN SOUTH AFRICA'S COMMUNICATION TO THE FIVE DATED 12 SEPTEMBER 1978 IT WAS STATED THAT SOUTH AFRICA "IS WILLING TO CONFIRM THAT THE MOMENT SWAPO UNDERTAKES TO STOP VIOLENCE AND IN FACT CARRIES OUT ITS UNDERTAKING, ACTION AGAINST SWAPO BY THE SOUTH AFRICAN FORCES WOULD CEASE". IT WAS SUGGESTED IN THE ABOVE MENTIONED AIDE MEMOIRE OF THE FIVE THAT SOUTH AFRICA SHOULD PROCLAIM ITS WILLINGESS TO CONFIRM ITS UNDERTAKING IN THIS REGARD IN A FORMAL MANNER.

TO GIVE EFFECT TO THIS THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT HAS TODAY INSTRUCTED ITS ACTING PERMANENT REPRESENTATIVE TO THE UN TO TRANSMIT TO THE SECRETARY-GENERAL FOR CIRCULATION AS A DOCUMENT OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL THE RELEVANT EXTRACT FROM THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT'S COMMUNICATION OF 12 SEPTEMBER 1978 TO THE FIVE. HE HAS ALSO BEEN INSTRUCTED TO INFORM THE SECRETARY-GENERAL THAT THE COMMUNICATION SERVES TO CONFIRM SOUTH AFRICA'S UNDERTAKING CONCERNING THE CESSATION OF VILENCE.

OUTSTANDING ISSUES THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT TAKES NOTE OF THE STATEMENT BY THE FIVE THAT SWAPO HAS ACCEPTED THEIR PROPOSAL. THIS CONTENTION HOWEVER DOES NOT RHYME WITH MR. NUJOMA'S SUBSEQUENT STATEMENT IN AN INTERVIEW IN NEW YORK IN WHICH HE SAID THAT WHILE SWAPO ACCEPTED THE SECRETARY-GENERAL'S REPORT, THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE WAS NOT ACCEPTABLE. MOREOVER, SWAPO HAS CONTINUED UNABATEDLY WITH ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA. THESE ACTS, TOGETEHR WITH THE RECENT STATEMENT BY MR.

NUJOMA, AND THE ASSASSINATION OF ITS POLITICAL OPPOINENTS, WOULD SEEM CONCLUSIVELY TO INDICATE THAT SWAPO HAS NO INTENTION OF WORKING TOWARDS A PEACEFUL TRANSITION TO INDEPENDENCE IN SOUTH WEST AFRICA. INDEED, SWAPO SEENS INTENT UPON WRECKING A PEACEFUL SETTLEMENT BY WAY OF MURDER, KIDNAPPING, ARMED ROBBERY AND OTHER FORMS OF INTIMIDATION DIRECTED, FOR THE MOST PART, AGAINST CIVILIANS. THE EXCHANGES BETWEEN SOUTH AFRICA AND THE FIVE HAVE CONTAINED SUGGESTIONS THAT UNTAG MAY NOT REACH THE NUMBER OF 7500. NEVERTHELESS THESE SUGGESTIONS HAVE INVARIABLY BEEN ACCOMPANIED BY ATTEMPTS TO JUSTIFY THIS FIGURE.

MOREOVER IT IS CLEAR THAT THIS FIGURE ALSO CAME AS A SURPRISE TO THOSE WHO HAVE NEGOTIATED WITH US OVER THE LAST YEAR AND A HALF. DURING GHE LENGTHY NEGOTIATIONS THE FIVE WERE REPEATEDLY REMINDED OF THE POLITICAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL EFFECT OF SUCH A LARGE NUMBER OF UN PERSONNEL ON THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA IN CIRCUMSTANCES WHERE THE IMPARTIALITY OF THE UN IS RENDERED SUSPECT BY ITS CONTINUED AND SUSTAINED ASSISTANCE TO SWAPO TO THE EXCLUSION OF ALL OTHER POLITICAL PARTIES IN SOUTH WEST AFRICA.

THUS, FOR EXAMPLE, SWAPO IS RECOGNIZED BY THE UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY AS "THE SOLE AND AUTHENTIC REPRESENTATIVE OF THE PEOPLE" OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA AND RECEIVES CONSIDERABLE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE. FURTHERMORE IT ENJOYS EXTENSIVE FACILITIES TO BEAM PROPAGANDA TO THE TERRITORY AND ELSEWHERE. INDED THE UN'S WHOLE INFORMATION SYSTEM ITSELF SUPPORTS SWAPO. WHILE SOUTH AFRICA HAS RECEIVED ASSURANCES ON THE COMPOSITION OF UNTAG, THERE IS NOW REASON FOR SERIOUS CONCERN ALSO ON THIS POINT. DURING THE NEGOTIATIONS SOUTH AFRICA MADE IT CLEAR THAT IT COULD NOT ACCEPT PERSONNEL FROM COUNTRIES WHICH HAVE BEEN SUPPORTING SWAPO'S HOSTILE ACTION. SOUTH AFRICA WAS IN NO SENSE OPPOSED TO CONTINGENTS FROM AFRICA AS SUCH.

IN FACT, DURING THE NEGOTIATIONS, IT MENTIONED SEVERAL SUCH COUNTRIES WHICH WOULD NOT BE DISQUALIFIED ON GROUNDS OF PRO-SWAPO COMMITMENTS. RECENTLY, HOWEVER, RELIABLE INFORMATION HAS REACHED THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT THAT IT IS PROBABLE THAT FORCES FROM AT LEAST ONE, AND POSSIBLY TWO COUNTRIES WILL BE INCLUDED WHICH WOULD NEGATE THE ASSURANCES RECEIVED. BEARING IN MIND OUR EXPERIENCE OF NON-CONSULATION ON THE SIZE OF THE UN FORCE, YOU WILL APPRECIATE THAT WE HAVE NO REASON TO BELIEVE THAT OUR VIEWS ON COMPOSITION WILL BE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT IN ANY EVENTUAL CONSULTATIONS WHICH MIGHT TAKE PLACE.

SOUTH AFRICA REMAINS WILLING TO WORK FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL WHICH IS ACCEPTED ON 25 APRIL 1978. FROM THE FIVE'S AIDE MEMOIRE IT IS CLEAR THAT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL IS LIKELY TO FOUNDER ON THE DIVERGENCE BETWEEN THE PROPOSAL AND THE SECRETARY-GENERL'S REPORT. THIS IS AGGRAVATED BY THE PROSPECT THAT BECAUSE OF THE DELAY THAT HAS OCCURRED SINCE THE ACCEPTANCE OF THE PROPOSAL THE HOLDING OF ELECTIONS MIGHT NOT TAKE PLACE BEFORE LATE NEXT YEAR. SUCH A POSSIBILITY IS FORESHADOWED IN THE SECRETARY-GENERAL'S COMMENTS AS WELL AS IN PARAGRAPH 6 OF THE FIVE'S AIDE-MEMOIRE DATED 16 SEPTEMBER.

IN VIEW OF SOUTH AFRICA'S ASSURANCES TO THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA THIS WILL DESTROY SOUTH AFRICA'S CREDIBILITY. IT SHOULD ALSO BE BORNE IN MIND THAT WHEN THE TURNHALLE REPRESENTATIVES IN AUGUST 1976 REQUESTED INDEPENDENCE BY THE 31ST DECEMBER 1978, OTHER PARTIES IN SOUTH WEST AFRICA REGARDED THAT DATE AS BEING TOO FAR IN THE FUTURE, AND ALLEGED THAT IT WAS A SOUTH AFRICAN SUBTERFUGE TO RETAIN ITS POSITION IN THE TERRITORY. A SUBSTANTIAL NUMBER OF THE POPULATION INSISTS THAT IT IS NOT FOR SOUTH AFRICA NOR FOR THE FIVE NOR FOR THE UNITED NATIONS, BUT FOR THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA TO DECIDE THEIR FUTURE.

THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA HAVE CLEARLY SIGNIFIED THEIR INALIENABLE RIGHT TO SELF-DETERMINATION AND INDEPENDENCE. THUS MORE THAN 85 PERCENT OF THE ESTIMATED ELIGIBLE VOTERS IN THE TERRITORY HAVE ENTHUSIASTICALLY REGISTERED TO VOTE, THIS NOTWITHSTANDING INTIMIDATION FROM CERTAIN QUARTERS NOT TO DO SO. THE QUESTION BEING RAISED WITH INCREASING INSISTENCE IS: WHO REALLY REPRESENTS THE PEOPLE OF THE TERRITORY? THIS IN ITSELF ADDS ANOTHER PRESSING REASON WHY ELECTIONS CANNOT BE DELAYED LONGER. THE TIME HAS COME FOR THE PEOPLE TO ELECT REPRESENTATIVES WHO CAN SPEAK AUTHORITATIVELY ON THEIR BEHALF.

CONCLUSIONS TO BE DRAWN THE LATEST EFFORTS HAVE CLEARLY NOT SUCCEEDED IN OVERCOMING THE DIFFICULTIES RAISED IN SOUTH AFRICA'S MESSAGE OF 12 SEPTEMBER 1978. SOUTH AFRICA THEREFORE HAS NO ALTERNATIVE BUT TO GIVE THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA THE OPPORTUNITY TO ELECT REPRESENTATIVES ON THE BASIS OF ONE-MAN-ONE-VOTE, COUNTRYWIDE, IN ORDER TO SETTLE WHOSE CLAIMS TO SPEAK FOR THE PEOPLE ARE JUSTIFIED. ALL OPTIONS WILL BE OPEN TO THEM. THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PRESCRIBE TO THEM.

THE BODY TO BE ELECTED MAY IN ADDITION: DECIDE TO DRAW UP A CONSTITUTION OR POSTPONE THE DRAFTING THEREOF; DECIDE TO PROCEED WITH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE; DECIDE TO ACCEPT THE SECRETARY-GENERAL'S REPORT. IT WILL BE OPEN TO THEM TO EXPRESS THEMSELVES ON NUMEROUS OTHER MATTERS. WHAT IS IMPORTANT IS THAT THE PEOPLE WILL HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO EXPRESS THEMSELVES ON ALL THE CONTROVERSIAL ISSUES WHICH THREATEN TO MAKE IMPOSSIBLE THE IMPLENENTATION OF THE FIVE'S PROPOSAL. PRETORIA 20 SEPTEMBER 1978 EDMONDSON

1978STATE242479.subject: NAMIBIA: INFORMAL SECURITY COUNCIL CONSULTATION SEPTEMBER 21

segments.text: SEPTEMBER 21

SUMMARY: THE SECURITY COUNCIL MET IN INFORMAL CONSULTATION PM SEPTEMBER 21 TO DISCUSS NAMIBIA. IN THE ABSENCE OF A FORMAL AFRICAN POSITION (THE AFRICAN GROUP IS SCHEDULED TO MEET SEPTEMBER 22), THE COUNCIL AGREED TO HOLD ANOTHER INFORMAL CONSULTATION ON MONDAY, SEPTEM?34 25. END SUNMARY.

IN RESPONSE TO AN AFRICAN GROUP REQUEST MADE PRIOR TO SOUTH AFRICA'S SEPTEMBER 20 ANNOUNCEMENT ON NAMIBIA, THE SECURITY COUNCIL HELD AN INFORMAL CONSULTATION ON NAMIBIA HM SEPTEMBER 21. AT THE OUTSET OF THE MEETING, MAURITIUS AMBASSADOR RAMPHUL STATED THAT THE AFRICAN GROUP HAD YET TO DISCUSS THE SOUTH AFRICAN ANNOUNCEMENT BUT WOULD $O SO TOMORROW. HE THEREFORE INDICATED THAT HE WOULD HAVE NO FORMAL VIEWS TO EXPRESS AT THE PRESENT TIME, AND HIS TWO AFRICAN COLLEAGUES TOOK THE SAME POSITION.

NIGERIAN MBASSADOR HARRIMAN URGED THE FIVE TO CONTINUE TO SUPPORT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL BUT ADDED THAT "PRESSURE WOULD HAVE TO BE BROUGHT TO BEAR". "WE WERE PROMISED A CARROT AND STICK APPROACH", HE WENT ON, "AND WE HAVE HAD ONLY THE CARROT".

AMBASSADOR MCHENRY THEN MADE CLEAR THE U.S. POSITION, WHICH WAS ENDORSED SUBSEQUENTLY BY EACH OF THE FIVE. THE UNITED STATES SUPPORTS THE FIVE'S PROPOSAL, HE REITERATED, AS WELL AS THE SECRETARY GENERAL'S REPORT, WHICH, HE OBSERVED, WAS CONSISTENT WITH THE PROPOSAL. IN CONSULTATION WITH THE AFRICAN GROUP AND THE FIVE, MCHEN Y ADDED, THE US WOULD BE FORMULATING ITS POSITION WITHOUT DELAY ON HOW BEST TO BRING ABOUT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL.

IN ENCOURAGING THE COUNCIL TO AWAIT THE VIEWS OF THE AFRICAN GROUP, INDIAN AMBASSADOR JAIPAL EXPRESSED HIS CONCERN THAT SOUTH AFRICA HAS DECIDED TO GO ON AHEAD UNILATERALLY AND ADDED THAT IF THAT IS THE CASE THE COUNCIL MUST CONSIDER CAREFULLY WHAT ACTION IT WILL TAKE. KUWAITI AMBASSADOR BISHARA EXPRESSED SIMILAR CONCERN FOR THE GRAVITY OF THE SITUATION AND EMPHASIZED THAT IF THE COUNCIL WISHED TO PROCEED WITH ADOPTION OF THE SECRETARY GENERAL'S REPORT, IT SHOULD DO SO IN THE CLEAR KNOWLEDGE THAT THE COUNCIL WILL LATER BE CALLED UPON TO ENFORCE IT.

WITH THE CALM AND UNCONTENTIOUS MEETING RESULTING IN AGREEMENT THAT NOTHING COULD BE DONE IN THE ABSENCE OF AFRICAN GROUP VIEWS, THE COUNCIL QUICKLY ACCEPTED AN FRG PROPOSAL THAT ANOTHER INFORMAL CONSULTATION BE HELD ON MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 25. THE PRECISE HOUR WILL BE DETERMINED BY THE SECURITY COUNCIL PRESIDENT, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT MONDAY'S ALREADY HECTIC SCHEDULE OF UNGA GENERAL DEBATE. BEFORE THE MEETING ADJOURNED SECRETARY GENERAL WALDHEIM, WITH EVIDENT CONCERN, EXPRESSED HIS HOPE THAT THE COUNCIL WOULD "AVOID TAKING A DECISION TO IMPLEMENT A RESOLUTION WHICH CANNOT YET BE IMPLEMENTED". ALL OF THE COUNCIL SEEMED TO APPRECIATE HIS CONCERN. YOUNG UNQUOTE CHRISTOPHER OIRG DIST: IO/ISO,REBU,SSO,NSCE,INRE,ICAE,NSC-$,ICA-$,POLI,HA,ACDA.

ALTHOUGH NOT A FORMAL OR OPENLY CATEGORICAL REJECTION OF THE UN PLAN, VORSTER'S STATEMENT INDICATES THAT THE SAG HAS SET ITS COURSE AND BLOCKED A RETURN TO THE INTERNATIONAL TRACK IS FOR THE FORESEEABLE FUTURE. IT IS CONCEIVABLE THAT THE SAG HAS BEEN PLAYING A CHARADE FROM THE BEGINNING AND EXPECTED ALL ALONG THAT IT WOULD GO THIS ROUTE. THAT IS POSSIBLE, BUT I DO NOT BELIEVE THIS IS THE CASE AND SUSPECT THAT THE TIDE SHIFTED SOMETIME IN THE PAST MONTH, I.E. AFTER AHTISARRI'S DEPARTURE FROM WINDHOEK.

THE CABINET PLUNGE TOWARD A HARD LINE APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN SHAPED TO A LARGE EXTENT BY VORSTER'S ILL HEALTH AND THE RELATED SUCCESSION STRUGGLE, WHICH UNEXPECTEDLY AND UNFORTUNATELY LOOMED ON THE STAGE AT THE CRITICAL MOMENT IN THE NAMIBIAN NEGOTIATIONS. ACCORDING TO SOME OF OUR VERLIGTE AFRIKANER SOURCES, P.W. BOTHA AND HIS ALLIES APPARENTLY EXPLOITED VORSTER'S ABSENCE AND THE ISSUE OF 7500 TROOPS AND LOCAL WHITE REACTION TO RECENT TERRORIST ACTIONS IN RHODESIA AND THE KATIMA MALILO INCIDENT IN AUGUST TO SEIZE THE INITIATIVE ON THE NAMIBIAN QUESTION.

CONNIE MULDER ALSO APPARENTLY JUMPED ON BOARD THE STEAMROLLER AS EVIDENCED BY HIS TIRADE AT THE TRANSVAAL PARTY CONGRESS AGAINST NEGOTIATING WITH MARXIST TERRORISTS. THE LACK OF LEADERSHIP FROM THE AILING VORSTER AND PIK'S CONCERN WITH HIS OWN CANDIDACY TO REPLACE HIM CONTRIBUTED SUBSTANTIALLY TO P.W.'S SUCCESS. MANY NATIONALISTS BELIEVE THAT TODAY'S DECISION WILL BE SEEN WITHIN SOUTH AFRICA AS A DEFEAT FOR PIK AND WILL GIVE MOMENTUM TO PW'S CANDIDACY.

BY ASSERTING THAT THE ELECTED CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY WOULD BE FREE TO ACCEPT THE WALDHEIM PLAN IF IT WISHED, THE SAG IS IN EFFECT PUTTING FORTH THE ELECTIONS AS A REFERENDUM WHICH WOULD ALLOW THE PEOPLE OF NAMIBIA TO DECIDE THE QUESTION. THE CABINET PRESUMABLY MADE ITS DECISION ON THE BASIS OF AN ASSESSMENT THAT THE SAG WOULD BE ABLE TO MANAGE A TURNOUT OF A MAJORITY OF VOTERS IN THE ELECTION, AND AS A RESULT, THE ASSEMBLY WOULD HAVE SOME CREDIBILITY AMONG WESTERN AUDIENCES AS A LEGITIMATE REPRESENTATIVE INSTITUTION.

PW AND OTHERS IN THE CABINET WHO CARRIED THE DAY ALSO VERY LIKELY BELIEVE THAT THE MILITARY, POLITICAL, AND ECONOMIC SITUATION IN NAMIBIA PROVIDE REASONABLY GOOD PROSPECTS THAT THE SAG CAN EMERGE SUCCESSFULLY FROM A CONFRONTATION WITH THE WORLD OVER THIS ISSUE, DESPITE THE NEAR-TERM RISK OF SANCTIONS AND ESCALATING CONFLICT.

1978STATE242481.subject: NAMIBIA: MEETING WITH AMBASSADORS OF FRONTLINE STATES AND NIGERIA

segments.text: AMBASSADOR MCHENRY AND MISOFFS EXCHANGED VIEWS ON NAMIBIA WITH AMBASSADORS OF FRONTLINE STATES PLUS NIGERIA AT USUN SEPTEMBER 21. MCHENRY OPENED THE MEETING BY OUTLINING THE PRELIMINARY REACTION OF THE FIVE TO THE SOUTH AFRICAN ANNOUNCEMENT, INDICATING THAT THE FIVE WERE INCLINED TO CALL FOR EARLY SECURITY COUNCIL ADOPTION OF THE SYG'S REPORT.

HE THEN ASKED THE AFRICANS FOR THEIR VIEWS ON NEXT STEPS, AND SPECIFICALLY MENTIONED THREE DIFFERING COURSES OF ACTION WHICH HAD BEEN SUGGESTED TO HIM BY AFRICANS HE HAD ALREADY CONSULTED WITH: (1) THAT THE SECURITY COUNCIL SHOULD ADOPT THE SYG'S REPORT AND FACE THE ENFORCEMENT QUESTION WHEN IT COMES UP; (2) THAT THE SC SHOULD CONSIDER IMMEDIATE ENFORCEMENT ACTION; AND (3) THAT IT WOULD BE A WASTE OF TIME TO ADOPT ANOTHER SC (PAPER) RESOLUTION WITHOUT ENFORCEMENT PROVISIONS AND THEREFORE THE COUNCIL SHOULD DO NOTHING AND SWAPO WILL SIMPLY CONTINUE THE ARMED STRUGGLE. (THIS THIRD ALTERNATIVE WAS SUGGESTED TO US BY SWAPO -REFTEL.)

ON THE GENERAL QUESTION OF NEXT STEPS, THE AFRICANS MADE IT VERY CLEAR THAT THEY BELIEVED IT WAS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE FIVE TO MOVE AHEAD TO SECURITY COUNCIL ADOPTION OF THE SYG'S REPORT, AND THAT THE FIVE MUST BE PREPARED TO AGREE TO CHAPTER VII SANCTIONS IF SOUTH AFRICA ATTEMPTED TO BLOCK IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NAMIBIA PROPOSALS. THE AMBASSADORS STATED THAT THEY HAD COOPERATED WITH THE FIVE IN GOOD FAITH, THAT THEY HAD DELIVERED SWAPO, AND THAT IT WAS NOW UP TO THE FIVE TO DELIVER SOUTH AFRICA.

IF THE FIVE WERE NOT PREPARED TO FOLLOW THROUGH WITH THEIR OWN INITIATIVE, THEY RISKED LOSING THE FUTURE COOPERATION OF THE FRONTLINE IN SEEKING NEGOTIATED SETTLEMENTS NOT ONLY IN NAMIBIA, BUT ELSEWHERE IN SOUTHERN AFRICA. A BRIEF EXCHANGE CONCERNING WESTERN CREDIBILITY ON RHODESIA SUGGESTED THAT THEIR REACTION WAS INFLUENCED BY A BELIEF, EXPRESSED BY NIGERIAN PERMREP HARRIMAN, THAT THE US/UK HAD ALSO FAILED TO MAKE GOOD ON THEIR "PROMISE TO BRING DOWN SMITH". THE FRONTLINE AMBASSADORS MADE CLEAR THEIR CONCERN THAT THE CREDIBILITY OF THEIR COUNTRIES AMONG FELLOW AFRICANS WAS ALSO AT STAKE IF THE FIVE FAILED TO FOLLOW THROUGH WITH THEIR NAMIBIA INITIATIVE.
HAVING AIDED IN A WESTERN EFFORT WHICH OTHER AFRICANS CONSIDERED A WASTE OF TIME, THEY NOW FELT "OUT ON A LIMB".

AMBASSADOR SALIM OF TANZANIA PARTICULARLY EMPAHSIZED THAT THE FRONTLINE HAD AGREED TO COOPERATE ON NAMIBIA UNDER THE ASSUMPTION THAT THE WEST, FOR THE FIRST TIME, WAS PREPARED TO UNDERTAKE AN IMPORTANT AFRICAN INITIATIVE AT THE SECURITY COUNCIL, AND THAT, IF THE NEGOTIATIONS FAILED, THROUGH NO FAULT OF SWAPO OR THE FRONTLINE, THE FIVE WOULD USE THEIR POWER AND INFLUENCE TO ENSURE SOUTH AFRICAN COMPLIANCE. HE STATED THAT SOUTH AFRICA HAD DIRECTLY REBUFFED THE WESTERN FIVE, AND THAT FOR THE SC TO DO NOTHING WOULD BE THE HEIGHT OF CYNICISM.

HE ADDED THAT SUCH CYNICISM COULD LEAD TO A NEGATIVE REACTION ON THE PART OF AFRICANS TO ALL INITIATIVES OF THE WESTERN FIVE. SALIM STRESSED REPEATEDLY THAT IT WAS NECESSARY FOR THE CREDIBILITY OF THE FIVE THAT THEY FOLLOW THROUGH TO A CONCLUSION ON THEIR OWN PROPOSAL ON NAMIBIA.

AMBASSADOR HARRIMAN OF NIGERIA REITERATED HIS BELIEF THAT SOUTH AFRICA WAS THE KEY TO ALL THE PROBLEMS OF SOUTHERN AFRICA, THAT IT WAS TIME TO CARRY ON WITH THE SYG'S REPORT, AND THAT IF SOUTH AFRICA BLOCKED ITS IMPLEMENTATION, CHAPTER VII SANCTIONS MUST BE ADOPTED. AMBASSADOR TLOU OF BOTSWANA ADVISED THAT IT WOULD BE EASIER FOR THE FIVE TO NEGOTIATE WITH THE AFRICANS IF THE AFRICANS KNEW THAT THE FIVE HAD A FIRM STRATEGY SHOULD SOUTH AFRICA REFUSE TO COOPERATE. HE SUGGESTED THAT, IN ADOPTING THE SYG'S REPORT, A PARAGRAPH BE INCLUDED IN THE RESOLUTION CALLING FOR SC ACTION (I.E. SANCTIONS) SHOULD SOUTH AFRICA BALK.
THE ANGOLAN AND MOZAMBICAN AMBASSADORS ENDORSED THE VIEWS EXPRESSED BY THEIR COLLEAGUES.

THE MEETING WAS CONSTRUCTIVE, CANDID AND POLITE. NONETHELESS, THE FEELING OF DEEP FRUSTRATION AMONG THE AFRICANS AND ANGER AT THE LATEST TURN OF EVENTS WAS VERY EVIDENT. THE AFRICAN AMBASSADORS MADE IT PLAIN THAT THE AFRICAN GROUP HAD NOT YET ADDRESSED THE QUESTION; THUS THEY WERE SPEAKING ONLY FOR THEMSELVES AT THIS TIME. (COMMENT. THE AFRICAN GROUP WILL MEET TOMORROW MORNING SEPTEMBER 22 ON NAMIBIA. THE ABOVE VIEWS OF THE FRONTLINE WILL BE MODERATE COMPARED TO OTHERS CERTAIN TO BE EXPRESSED THEN.) YOUNG UNQUOTE CHRISTOPHER

1978STATE242482.subject: NAMIBIA: DRAFT WESTERN FIVE AIDE MEMOIRE TO SOUTH AFRICA THE CONTACT GROUP APPROVED AD REFERENDUM SEPTEMBER

segments.text: SOUTH AFRICA THE CONTACT GROUP APPROVED AD REFERENDUM SEPTEMBER 12 THE FOLLOWING DRAFT OF AN AIDE MEMOIRE TO THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT PROPOSED FOR DELIVERY SIMULTANEOUSLY WITH THE DRAFT FOREIGN MINISTERS' MESSAGE (SEPTEL): BEGIN TEXT: MATTERS RAISED IN THE COMMUNICATION FROM THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT TO THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE FIVE GOVERNMENTS IN NEW YORK ON 12 SEPTEMBER CESSATION OF VIOLENCE

THE BASIC REQUIREMENT FOR IMPLEMENTING THE PROPOSAL OF THE GOVERNMENTS OF THE FIVE IS THE COMPREHENSIVE CESSATION OF ALL HOSTILE ACTS. THE FIVE THEREFORE NOTE WITH SATISFACTION THE RECOGNITION CONTAINED IN YOUR NOTE THAT THIS IS AN ESSENTIAL PREREQUISITE, AND YOUR UNDERTAKING TO ABIDE BY A CEASEFIRE. HOWEVER WE CONSIDER IT NECESSARY THAT THE CEASEFIRE SHOULD BE PROCLAIMED IN A FORMAL MANNER. WE BELIEVE THAT THE MOST APPROPRIATE METHOD WOULD BE SOLEMN AND BINDING DECLARATIONS OF A CEASEFIRE.

THESE SHOULD BE SIGNED SEPARATELY BY BOTH PARTIES ON INDENTICALLY WORDED PIECES OF PAPER AND DELIVERED TO THE SECRETARY GENERAL FOR CIRCULATION, AS YOU SUGGEST, AS A DOCUMENT OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL AT THE TIME OF THE PASSAGE OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION IMPLEMENTING THE PROPOSAL.

THE LETTER DATED 8 SEPTEMBER FROM MR. NUJOMA TO THE SECRETARY GENERAL IS A CLEAR PUBLIC STATEMENT OF SWAPO'S ACCEPTANCE OF THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE. MOREOVER SWAPO IS PREPARED TO SIGN A SOLEMN AND BINDING DECLARATION OF A CEASEFIRE. II. OUTSTANDING ISSUES

WE ARE ASSURED THAT "THE AREAS OF CONCERN" FOR SWAPO IN THE REPORT OF THE SECRETARY GENERAL WILL BE OVERCOME BY THE POINTS OF CLARIFICATION WHICH THE SECRETARY GENERAL INTENDS TO MAKE IN HIS INTRODUCTION AT THE COUNCIL OF HIS REPORT. THUS THEIR ACCEPTANCE OF THE REPORT IS NO LONGER CONDITIONAL. WHILE WE DEPLORE CONTINUING ACTS OF VIOLENCE, THE SUREST WAY TO BRING THE VIOLENCE TO AN END IS QUICKLY TO TAKE ACTION TO IMPLEMENT OUR PROPOSAL ON THE LINES INDICATED IN THE SECRETARY GENERAL'S REPORT.

REGARDING THE SIZE OF UNTAG, WE HAVE ALWAYS MAINTAINED THAT OUR PROPOSAL, AS IT HAS EVOLVED, WOULD REQUIRE FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION A SUBSTANTIAL UN PRESENCE IN THE TERRITORY. FOR REASONS WELL KNOWN TO THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT, NO FIGURES FOR THE SITE OF UNTAG ARE CONTAINED IN OUR PROPOSAL. AS PARAGRAPH 8(E) OF OUR PROPOSAL STATES, "IN ESTABLISHING THE MILITARY SECTION OF UNTAG, THE SECRETARY GENERAL WILL KEEP IN MIND FUNCTIONAL AND LOGISTICAL REQUIREMENTS.

THE FIVE GOVERNMENTS, AS MEMBERS OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL, WILL SUPPORT THE SECRETARY GENERAL'S JUDGMENT IN HIS DISCHARGE OF THIS RESPONSIBILITY." WE ARE CONVINCED BY THE ARGUMENTS OF GENERAL PHILIPP THAT THE SIZE OF THE FORCE IS THE MINIMUM COMMENSURATE WITH THE TASKS LAID ON IT, BEARING IN MIND THE VERY LARGE AREA IN WHICH UNTAG WILL HAVE TO OPERATE AND THE ENORMOUS LOGISTICAL PROBLEMS. THE TASKS ARE THOSE SET OUT IN THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE AND ACCEPTED BY THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT.
HAVING REGARD TO THESE TASKS WE CANNOT AGREE THAT THIS SIZE OF FORCE COULD IN ANY WAY BE REGARDED AS AN OCCUPYING FORCE OR AS AN OPERATIONAL PEACEKEEPING FORCE.

REGARDING CONSULTATION ABOUT THE FORCE, WE CONSIDER THAT THE EXCHANGES WHICH HAVE TAKEN PLACE BETWEEN YOU AND US AND BETWEEN THE SECRETARY GENERAL AND YOU IN THE LAST WEEKS SINCE PUBLICATION OF THE SECRETARY GENERAL'S REPORT HAVE AMOUNTED TO A VERY SERIOUS AND CONTINUING PROCESS OF CONSULTATION. WE WOULD ALSO POINT OUT THAT THE SECRETARY GENERAL IN HIS REPORT STATES THAT IT IS HIS INTENTION TO CONSULT THE PARTIES CONCERNED ON THE COMPOSITION OF THE MILITARY COMPONENT. WE ARE CONFIDENT THAT YOUR VIEWS ON THE COMPOSITION WILL BE SOUGHT IN ADVANCE OF ANY FINAL DECISION ON THIS ISSUE.

WE NOTE THAT YOU STILL CONSIDER THAT THE FIGURE OF 360 FOR THE CIVIL POLICE ELEMENT OF UNTAG IS UNNECESSARILY LARG. THE CLARIFYING INTRODUCTORY REMARKS OF THE SECRETARY GENERAL INDICATE THAT HE WILL KEEP THE SIZE OF THIS ELEMENT UNDER CONTINOUS REVIEW.

LIKE YOU WE HAD HOPED THAT THE COMPLETION OF THE STEPS OUTLINED IN OUR PROPOSAL COULD LEAD TO INDEPENDENCE FOR NAMIBIA NO LATER THAN 31 DECEMBER 1978. UNFORTUNATELY THIS DATE, AS ORIGINALLY INCORPORATED IN OUR PROPOSAL, IS NO LONGER REALISTIC IN VIEW OF THE TIME REQUIRED FOR THE SUCCESSIVE STAGES LEADING TO ELECTIONS AS SET DOWN IN THE ANNEX TO OUR PROPOSAL. WE SHALL CONTINUE TO WORK FOR THE PROPER AND FULL IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL, BUT WE AGREE WITH THE SECRETARY GENERAL THAT THIS CANNOT NOW BE DONE BY THE END OF 1978.

WE APPRECIATE THAT THIS IS A PROBLEM FOR YOU, BUT WE MUST NOT LET THE PROPOSAL FAIL NOW BECAUSE THE REALITIES OF THE SITUATION DICTATE AN EXTENSION OF THE DATE OF ELECTIONS BY A FEW MONTHS. THE COUNTDOWN FOR THE STEPS NECESSARY TO IMPLEMENT THE PROPOSAL SHOULD START FROM THE DATE OF ESTABLISHMENT OF THE MANDATE, AS THE REPORT OF THE SECRETARY GENERAL PROPOSES.

WE AGREE THAT THE WISHES OF THE PEOPLE OF THE TERRITORY MUST BE RESPECTED AND THAT THE TIME HAS COME FOR THEM TO ELECT REPRESENTATIVES WHO CAN SPEAK AUTHORITATIVELY ON THEIR BEHALF THROUGH THE HOLDING OF FREE AND FAIR ELECTIONS WHICH WILL ATTRACT THE RECOGNITION OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY. THIS DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE MAINTENANCE OF A PARTICULAR DATE FOR THE HOLDING OF THOSE ELECTIONS BUT RATHER ON INTERNATIONAL ACCEPTANCE THAT THE CONDITIONS NECESSARY FOR FREE AND FAIR ELECTIONS HAVE BEEN MET. . YOUNG UNQUOTE CHRISTOPHER ORIG DIST: IO/AF,EUR,SS,SSO,SP,L,NSCE,PM

FOLLOWING IS THE TEXT OF STATEMENT ON NAMIBIA ISSUED BY PRIME MINISTER VORSTER AT 1430 LOCAL TIME ON 20 SEPTEMBER 1978: BEGIN TEXT: SOUTH WEST AFRICA NEVER FORMED PART OF THE TERRITORIAL SOVEREIGNTY OF SOUTH AFRICA. AS FROM 1920 THE TERRITORY WAS ADMINISTERED AS A MANDATED TERRITORY AND AFTER THE LEAGUE OF NATIONS WAS DISSOVLED IN 1946 SUCCESSIVE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT'S MADE IT THEIR POLICY TO CONTINUE ADMINISTERING SOUTH WEST AFRICA IN THE SPIRIT OF THE MANDATE I.E. THE TERRITORY SHOULD BE SO ADMINISTERED AS TO PROMOTE TO THE UTMOST THE MATERIAL AND MORAL WELL-BEING AND THE SOCIAL PROGRESS OF THE INHABITANTS.

THE EMPHASIS HAS THUS, AS FAR AS SOUTH AFRICA IS CONCERNED, THROUGHOUT BEEN PLACED ON THE FURTHERANCE OF THE INTERESTS OF THE INHIBITANTS OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA. THIS IS ALSO THE REASON WHY IT IS THE GOVERNMENT'S BASIC POINT OF DEPARTURE THAT THE INHABITANTS OF THE TERRITORY SHOULD THEMSELVES FREELY DECIDE ON THEIR POLITICAL FUTURE. THIS CORNERSTONE OF OUR POLICY WAS FORMULATED AS FOLLOWS TEN YEARS AGO IN AN OFFICIAL PUBLICATION, " SOUTH WEST AFRICA SURVEY 1967" WHICH WAS GIVEN WORLD WIDE DISTRIBUTION: " IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO EMBARK ON SPECULATION AS TO WHAT THE ULTIMATE FUTURE POLITICAL PATTER WILL BE - I.E.

WHETHER AND TO WHAT EXTENT THERE MAY BE AMALGAMATIONS OR UNIONS OF SOME KIND, FEDERATIONS, COMMONWEALTH OR COMMON MARKET ARRANGEMENTS ETC. THE PEOPLES THEMSELVES WILL ULTIMATELY DECIDE." THESE WERE INDEED PROPHETIC WORDS, ESPECIALLY WHEN IT IT TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT THAT THEY WERE WRITTEN IN 1967. THUS THE POLITICAL FUTURE OF THE TERRITORY LIES IN THE HANDS OF THE INHABITANTS. ALL OPTIONS ARE OPEN TO THEM. THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERMENT DOES NOT PRESCRIBE POLICY FOR SOUTH WEST AFRICA. THROUGH THE YEARS WE HAVE HONOURED THIS COMMITMENT AND ENCOURAGED AND ASSISTED THE PEOPLES OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA ON THE ROAD TO SELF-DETERMINATION.

IN AUGUST 1976 THE ELECTED REPRESENTATIVES OF THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA REQUESTED INDEPENDENCE BY 31 DECEMBER 1978. IN AN EFFORT TO RESOLVE THE 31 YEAR OLD DISPUTE WITH THE UNITED NATIONS OVER SOUTH WEST AFRICA AND ALSO IN THE HOPE OF REALISING INTERNATIONAL RECOGNITION FOR AN INDEPENDENT SOUTH WEST AFRICA, THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT, SEVENTEEN MONTHS AGO, ENTERED INTO NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE FIVE WESTERN POWERS IN THE SECURITY COUNCIL. IN THESE DISCUSSIONS EFFORTS WERE MADE TO RESOLVE THE ISSUES OF PRINCIPLE WHICH HAD IN THE PAST MADE A SOLUTION IMPOSSIBLE.

AS STATED BY ME IN WINDHOEK IN MAY 1975: PERHAPS THE SOUTH AFRICAN POSITION WAS NOT SO FAR REMOVED FROM THAT OF THE U.N. TO MAKE AGREEMENT IMPOSSIBLE. OVER THE YEARS THE MAIN ELEMENTS OF THE DISPUTE CENTERED AROUND THE FOLLOWING ISSUES: - A UNITARY STATE; - UNIVERSAL ADULT SUFFRAGE - THE REMOVAL OF DISCRIMINATION BASED ON COLOUR; - THE HOLDING OF FREE AND FAIR ELECTIONS; - THE URGENCY OF ACHIEVING INDEPENDENCE; - THE RIGHT OF ALL SOUTH WEST AFRICAN TO RETURN TO PARTICIPATE PEACEFULLY IN THE POLITICAL PROCESS; - THE RELEASE OF DETAINEES WHEREEVER HELD.

SOUTH AFRICA AS COMMITTED TISELF TO DOING ALL THIS AND HAS ALREADY GONE A LONG WAY TOWARDS MAKING POSSIBLE THE REALISATION OF THIS GOALS. IT IS THEREFORE A CAUSE OF GREAT CONCERN AND DISAPPOINTMENT TO THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT THAT, IN SPITE OF WHAT HAS BEEN ACHIEVED AND THE CLEAR WISHES OF THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA, WE ARE NOW CAUGHT UP IN ARGUMENTS FAR REMOVED FROM THE MAIN QUESTIONS OF PRINCIPLE.

I SAY THIS BECAUSE AS FAR BACK AS 25 APRIL 1978 MY GOVERNMENT ACCEPTED THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE WESTERN COUNTRIES, IN ITS FINAL AND DEFINITIVE FORM, IN GOOD FAITH AND IN TIME TO ALLOW FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSED SCHEDULE LEADING TO INDEPENDENCE. THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA EXPECTED THE EARLY IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL AND THEREAFTER INTERNATIONAL RECOGNITION OF AN INDEPENDENT SOUTH WEST AFRICA. IN TERMS OF SECURITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION 431 DATED 27 JULY 1978, ADOPTED ON THE WESTERN PROPOSAL, THE SECRETARY-GENERAL'S SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE VISITED SOUTH WEST AFRICA IN AUGUST 1978 FOR THE PURPOSE OF SUBMITTING A REPORT ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL.

DURING HIS VISIT HE RECEIVED THE FULL COOPERATION OF THE ADMINISTRATOR-GENERAL AND THE AUTHORITIES CONCERNED. THE SECRETARY-GENERAL'S REPORT TO THE SECURITY COUNCIL, BASED ON HIS SPECIAL REPRESENTATIVE'S RECOMMENDATIONS, DEVIATED SUBSTANTIALLY FROM THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE. THE MOST STRIKING DEVIATIONS CONCERNED; -THE SIZE OF THE U.N. MILITARY CONTINGENT; - THE INTRODUCTION OF A U.N. CIVIL POLICE COMPONENT; - THE LACK OF CONSULTATION WITH THE ADMINISTRATOR- GENERAL; - THE ELECTION DATE. I DO NOT WISH TO REFER EXTENSIVELY TO THESE MATTER, SINCE THEY HAVE ALL BEEN DEALT WITH IN COMMUNICATIONS ADDRESSED BY MY FOREIGN MINISTER TO THE SECRETARY-GENERAL AND THE FIVE, AS WELL AS IN DISCUSSIONS WITH THEM.

AS FAR AS THE U.N. MILITARY COMPONENT IS CONCERNED, IT SHOULD BE MADE ABSOLUTELY CLEAR THAT NEVER DURING THE DISCUSSIONS WITH THE FIVE WAS A FIGURE HIGHER THAN 3,000 MENTIONED BY THEM, AND SOUTH AFRICA FOR ITS PART HAD INDICATED THAT IT COOULD NOT ACCEPT A FIGURE EXCEEDING 2,000. IT WILL BE APPRECIATED THAT IN THESE CIRCUMSTANCES THE FIGURE OF 7,500 PUT FORWARD BY THE SECRETARYGENERAL CAME NOT ONLY AS A SURPIRSE BUT ALSO AS A SCHOCK. INDEED, I AM AWARE THAT THOSE WHO HAD BEEN NEGOTIATING WITH US ALL THIS TIME MUST HAVE BEEN EQUALLY SURPRISED.

THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA ARE NOW BEING CONFRONTED IN THE SECRETARY GENERAL'S REPORT WITH A MILTARY COMPONENT WHICH VIRTUALLY AMOUNTS TO AN OPERATIONAL PEACEKEEPING FORCE OR AN OCCUPATION FORCE. SOUTH AFRICA'S OBJECTION TO THIS FIGURE STEMS FROM THE FACT THAT THE GUIDING PRINCIPLE IN THE WESTERN PROPOSAL IN THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A VISIBLE PEACE. UNDER SUCH CIRCUMSTANCES THE NEED FOR A LARGE MILITARY PRESENCE IS OBVIATED AS, INDEED, THE FIVE POINTED OUT TO SOUTH AFRICA WHEN THEY SOUGHT A REDUCTION IN OUR TROOP NUMBERS. BY THE SAME TOKEN THE ORDER OF NUMBERS NOW BEING SUGGESTED BY THE SECRETARY-GENERAL IN HIS REPORT IS TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE TO SOUTH AFRICA.

DURING THE LENGTHY NEGOTIATIONS THE FIVE WERE REPEATEDLY REMINDED OF THE POLITICAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL EFFECT OF SUCH A LARGE NUMBER OF UN PERSONNEL ON THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA. THE IMPARTIALITY OF THE UN IS RENDERED SUSPECT BY THE CONTINUED AND SUSTAINED ASSISTANCE TO SWAPO TO THE EXCLUSION OF ALL OTHER POLITICAL PARTIES IN SOUTH WEST AFRICA. THUS, FOR EXAMPLE, SWAPO IS RECOGNIZED BY THE UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY AS " THE SOLE AND AUTHENTIC REPRESENTATIVE" OF THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA AND RECEIVES CONSIDERBALE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE. FURTHERMORE IT ENJOYS EXTENSIVE FACILITIES TO BEAM PROPAGANDA TO THE TERRITORY AND ELSEWHERE. INDEED THE UN'S WHOLE INFORMATION SYSTEM ITSELF SUPPORTS SWAPO.

THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE SPECIFICALLY DEFINES THAT DURING THE TRANSITIONAL PERIOD THE MAINTENANCE OF LAW AND ORDER WOULD REST WITH THE EXISTING POLICE FORCES. THERE IS NO PROVISION IN THE PROPOSAL FOR A UN POLICE CONTINGENT AS PROPOSED IN THE SECRETARY-GERNAL'S REPORT, AND WHILE SUBSEQUENT EXCHANGES WERE SOMEWHAT REASSURING IN THIS REGARD, THERE IS STILL AN INSISTENCE ON THE FIGURE OF 360 CIVIL POLICE- AN UNNECESSARILY HIGH NUMBER.

IN THE COURSE OF THE NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE FIVE, IT WAS OFTEN STRESSED THAT THE UNDERLYING IDEA WAS THAT THE ADMINSTRATORGENERAL AND THE REPRESENTATIVE OF THE SECRETARY-GENERAL SHOULD, IN KEEPING WITH THE VITAL REQUIREMENTS OF CLOSE COOPERATION AND MUTUAL TRUST, CONSULT EACH OTHER IN MANY FIELDS, INCLUDING THE COMPOSITION AND SIZE OF THE UN MILITARY COMPONENT. WE RECEIVED SPECIFIC ASSURANCES FROM THE FIVE IN THIS REGARD. NEVERTHELESS, NO SUCH CONSULTATION TTOK PLACE IN DETERMINING THE FIGURE OF 7,500, NOR HAS THERE AS YET BEEN ANY CONSULTATION ON THE COMPOSITION OF THE UN FORCES.

THE REPORT OF THE SECRETARY- GENERAL DOES NOT OFFER ANY REAL HOPE THAT IT MIGHT BE POSSIBLE TO REACH CONSENSUS ON THE TIMING OF ELECTIONS IN SOUTH WEST AFRICA. IN FACT, IT CREATES THE IMPRESSION THAT THE DATE FOR ELECTIONS IS UNIMPORTANT. A FULL THREE MONHS LAPSED AFTER SOUTH AFRICA'S ACCEPTANCE ON 25 APRIL BEFORE THE PROPSAL WAS, FOR THE FIRST TIME, REFERRED TO THE SECURITY COUNCIL. THIS IN ITSELF MADE IT IMPOSSIBLE TO ADHERE TO THE PROGRAMME ENVISAGED FOR THE ELECTORAL PROCESS AND AT THE SAME TIME TO OBSERVE THE INDEPENDENCE DATE. THIS DELAY WAS CAUSED BY SWAPO'S INTRANSIGENCE. THE FIVE TELL US SWAPO HAS ACCEPTED THEIR PROPOSAL.

IN FACT ONLY LAST WEEKEND NUJOMA REPUDIATED THE PROPOSAL. THE REASON IS THAT THE PROPOSAL PROVIDES FOR FREE ELECTIONS IN THE TERRITORY AND SWAPO HAS NO CONFIDENCE THAT IT CAN WIN AN ELECTION. SWAPO FEELS THE ONLY WAY IT CAN ASSURE ITSELF OF ASSUMING POWER IS BY DISORDER AND VIOLENCE. THE PROPOSAL DEFINITIVELY PROVIDES FOR ELECTIONS AND INDEPENDENCE BY 31 DECEMBER AT THE LATEST AND FOR A RUN-UP PERIOD OF SEVEN MONTHS BEFORE ELECTIONS. AS ALREADY STATED, THIS PROGRAMME WAS POSSIBLE WHEN SOUTH AFRICA ACCEPTED THE PROPOSAL. THE REGISTRATION OF VOTERS, A LONG-DRAWNOUT PROCESS WHICH SWAPO STRENOUSLY OPPOSED, HAS VIRTUALLY BEEN COMPLETED.

THE REGISTRATION OF VOTERS IS OPPOSED BY SWAPO AND OTHERS DESPITE SOUTH AFRICA'S WILLINGNESS TO ALLOW THE PROCESS TO BE FULLY EXAMINED BY THE UN. AGAIN THIS TESTIFIES TO SWAPO'S DELAYING TACTICS. SWAPO WANTS TO BUILD UP BASES AND SUPPLIES OF WEAPONS AND TO TRAIN TERRORISTS TO ATTACK WOUTH WEST AFRICA. SWAPO'S FIRM INTENTION IS TO KEEP ON DELAYING ELECTIONS. THE PEOPLE OF THE TERRITORY, HOWEVER , DO NOT WANT TO DELAY ELECTIONS. I REITERATE, SOUTH AFRICA HAS ALWAYS ACCEPTED THE PRINCIPLE THAT IT IS FOR THE PEOPLE THEMSELVES TO DETERMINE THEIR OWN FUTURE.

IT IS NOT FOR THE SECRETARY-GENERAL OR THE UNITED NATIONS OR ANY OTHER ENTITY TO DELAY THE PROCESS LEADING TO SELF-DETERMINATION AND INDEPENDENCE. SOUTH AFRICA ACCEPTED THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE IN GOOD FAITH, BUT NO-ONE CAN BLAME THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT FOR BEING UNWILLING TO ACCEPT EXTENDED AND AMENDED PROVISIONS OF A PROPOSAL WHICH WAS DESCRIBED TO US AS BEING FINAL AND DEFINITIVE. INDEED, THE FIVE PLEDGED THAT THEY WOULD STAND BY THEIR PROPOSAL. DURING THE PAST FEW DAYS THE MOST STRENUOUS EFFORTS WERE MADE BY THE SOUTH AFRICAN FOREIGN MINISTER AND THE FIVE TO OVERCOME THE DIFFERENCES. REGRETTABLY THESE EFFORTS HAVE NOT SUCCEEDED.

WHILE THE SOUTH AFRICAN GOVERNMENT DOES NOT WISH TO CLOSE DOORS, IT CANNOT ALLOW THIS IMPASSE TO CONTINUE INDEFINITELY. BEARING IN MIND THE CONSEQUENCES OF THESE DEVELOPMENTS FOR THE EPOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA AS WELL AS THOSE OF SOUTHERN AFRICA AS A WHOLE, THE GOVERNMENT HAS GIVEN ITS MOST SERIOUS ATTENTION TO ALL THE ALTERNATIVES. THE CABINET IN ITS DELIBERATIONS YESTERDAY CONCLUDED THAT THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA IN ACCORDANCE WITH THEIR WISHES WOULD HAVE TO BE GIVEN THE OPPORTUNITY TO ELECT THEIR OWN REPRESENTATIVES.

THIS WILL BE DONE ON THE BASIS OF UNIVERSAL ADULT SUFFRAGE IN COUNTRYWIDE ELECTIONS IN ORDER TO ESTABLISH UNEQUIVOCABLY WHO HAS THE RIGHT TO SPEAK FOR THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA. THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICA HAVE CLEARLY SIGNIFIED THEIR DESIRE TO EXERCISE THEIR INALIENABLE RIGHT TO SELF-DETERMINATION AND INDEPENDENCE. THUS MORE THAN 85 0/0 OF THE ESTIMATED ELIGIBLE VOTERS IN THE TERRITORY HAVE ENTHUSIATICALLY REGISTERED TO VOTE, THIS NOTWITHSTANDING INTIMIDATION FROM CERTAIN QUARTERS NOT TO DO SO. ALL OPTIONS REMAIN OPEN TO THEM. WE WILL NOT PRESCRIBE TO THEM.

THE BODY TO BE ELECTED MAY: - DECIDE TO DRAW UP A CONSTITUTION OR POSTPONE THE DRAFTING THEREOF; - DECIDE TO PROCEED WITH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSAL OF THE FIVE; - DECIDE TO ACCEPT THE SECRETARY-GENERAL'S REPORT. THEY WILL, OF COURSE, ALSO BE FREE TO EXPRESS THEMSELVES ON NUMEROUS OTHER MATTERS, WHICH WILL BE DEALT WITH IN THE RELEVANT PROCLAMATION TO BE ISSUED SHORTLY. . EDMONDSON UNQUOTE CHRISTOPHER ORIG DIST: AF/EUR,ISO,ICA-$,NSC-$,POLI,READ,ACDA,TRSE,OMB.

PIK BOTHA'S AIDE NEIL VAN HEERDEN TODAY (SEPT. 17) SUGGESTED TO POLITICAL COUNSELOR TAYLOR THAT THEY FLOAT THE IDEA TO THEIR REPECTIVE PRINCIPALS OF DELAYING SECURITY COUNCIL ACTION UNTIL AFTER SEPTEMBER 28 NATIONAL PARTY CAUCUS WHICH IS EXPECTED TO ELECT A NEW PRIME MINISTER AS WELL AS STATE PRESIDENT. VAN HEERDEN, CAUTIONING THAT THIS PROPOSAL SHOULD NOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO HIM, SAID THERE WAS "NO WAY" THE FOREIGN MINISTER COULD WIN CABINET AGREEMENT TO PROCEED WITH THE UN PLAN GIVEN THE CURRENT SCRAMBLE FOR SUCCESSION TO VORSTER AND THE PRESENT LAME DUCK LEADERSHIP.

AS HE HAD WITH BRITISH AMBASSADOR SCOTT YESTERDAY, VAN HEERDEN EMPHASIZED OVER AND OVER THAT THE CABINET WAS ADAMANTLY SET AGAINST THE 7,500 UN TROOP FIGURE. HE DESCRIBED THE SITUATION VARIOUSLY AS "BLACK", AS THE "END OF THE TUNNEL," AND AS "IN A DITCH". THE 7,5000 FIGURE, HE SAID, WAS AN OBSESSION WITH THE CABINET AS IT WAS SEEN AS THE FINAL EXAMPLE OF SOUTH AFRICA BEING "SUCKED IN", AND AT THE PRESENT TIME A MODUS VIVENDI WHICH RETAINED THE FORMAL COMMITMENT TO 7,500 WOULD NOT BE ACCEPTABLE.

TAYLOR SAID HE WAS EQUALLY PESSIMISTIC THAT WALDHEIM OR THE AFRICAN STATES, NOT TO SPEAK OF SWAPO, COULD BE PERSUADED SPECIFICALLY TO REDUCE THE FIGURE OF 7,500, AT LEAST AS THE MAXIMUM AUTHORIZED NUMBER. VAN HEERDEN REPLIED THAT HE UNDERSTOOD THIS AND THAT SOME MODUS VIVENDI MIGHT BE POSSIBLE IF EITHER FANIE BOTHA OR PIK BOTHA WON THE PREMIER STAKES. IT WOULD BE A TRAGEDY, HE ASSERTED, IF WE LOCKED OURSELVES INTO A FAILURE BEFORE A NEW LEADERSHIP WAS FORMED. "IT WILL MAKE A WORLD OF DIFFERENCE WHO WINS ON SEPTEMBER 28," VAN HEERDEN SAID.

ACCORDING TO VAN HEERDEN, CAMPAIGNING BEHIND THE SCENES IS NOW FIERCE; TELEPHONES ARE RINGING ALL OVER THE COUNTRY. IT IS "DEFINITE" THAT VORSTER WILL REVEAL THIS WEEK THAT HE IS EITHER STEPPING UP TO THE PRESIDENCY OR RETIRING. TAYLOR SAID HE HAD HEARD THAT FOREIGN MINISTER WAS ENGAGED IN A SERIOUS CAMPAIGN FOR THE TOP SPOT. VAN HEERDED NODDED AND SAID THE FOREIGN MINISTER HAD A "REAL CHANCE".

TAYLOR PROBED ABOUT RUMORS OF SOME PERSONAL AFFAIR WHICH MIGHT EMBARRASS FANIE. VAN HEERDEN REPLIED THAT HE HAD HEARD OF THESE RUMORS AND HE SPECULATED THAT FANIE WAS NOT KEEN FOR THE JOB. THE LABOR MINISTER, ACCORDING TO VAN HEERDEN, IS A CLOSE PERSONAL FRIEND OF PIK'S AND "IT WOULD BE BETTER FOR FANIE TO WITHDRAW NOW IN FAVOR OF PIK THAN TO BE TRIPPED UP AT THE LAST MOMENT BY EMBARRASSING REVELATIONS." PIK, WITH FANIE'S SUPPORT, HE THOUGHT, COULD "MAKE IT." MULDER WAS OUT OF IT, HE SAID, AND P.W. BOTHA WAS SIMPLY NOT LIKED.

GIVEN THE POLITICAL SITUATION, VAN HEERDEN SAID, IT WOULD NOT BE POSSIBLE FOR FOREIGN MINISTER TO PROPOSE THAT THE SAG SEEK A DELAY IN FINAL CONSIDERATION OF THE UN PLAN. IT WOULD BE BEST FOR SUCH A PROPOSAL TO COME FROM THE WESTERN SIDE; PERHAPS OWEN COULD SUGGEST IT IF HE MAKES HIS PROPOSED TRIP TO PRETORIA. THE FOREIGN MINISTER COULD THEN PUT IT TO THE CABINET AS A WESTERN IDEA AND PROBABLY WIN AGREEMENT.

VAN HEERDEN ALSO DISCUSSED RADIO REPORTS TODAY QUOTING SAM NUJOM AS REJECTING THE WESTERN PROPOSAL AND SAYING SWAPO WOULD ONLY ACCEPT A UN PLAN WHICH CALLED FOR A CEASEFIRE, A RE-REGISTRATION OF VOTERS, AND A SECURITY COUNCIL VETO OVER THE ADMINISTRATOR-GENERAL. VAN HEERDEN SAID NUJOMA WOULD EITHER HAVE TO BACK DOWN OR WITHDRAW FROM THE AGREEMENT; EITHER WAY SOUTH AFRICA WINS.

COMMENT: WE ARE INCLINED TO ACCEPT VAN HEERDEN'S JUDGMENT OF THE UNLIKELIHOOD OF RECEIVING A POSITIVE CABINET RESPONSE DURING THE CURRENT POLITICAL CRISIS. WE HAVE NOT DISCUSSED THIS WITH THE PRETORIA FIVE YET, BUT BELIEVE THEY WOULD LIKELY AGREE WITH RECOMMENDATION THAT THE CONTACT GROUP CONSULT WITH WALDHEIM AND THE AFRICAN STATES ON WAYS OF DELAYING A SECURITY COUNCIL MEETING ON NAMIBIA UNTIL THE BEGINNING OF NEXT MONTH. AS VAN HEERDEN POINTED OUT, PERHAPS ONLY 10 DAYS FURTHER DELAY WILL MAKE THE DIFFERENCE.

NUJOMA'S REPORTED REMARKS ARE NOT HELPFUL. HARD LINERS IN THE SAG COULD WELL USE THESE LATEST COMMENTS AS BOTH JUSTIFYING AND RATIONALIZING A SAG DECISION TO MOVE AHEAD UNILATERALLY. ON THE OTHER HAND, PERHAPS THEY COULD BE USED TO JUSTIFY AN ARGUMENT TO THE AFRICANS THAT THE ISSUE CANNOT BE TAKEN TO THE SECURITY COUNCIL YET.

SABC RADIO, SEPTEMBER 21, BROADCAST STATEMENT OF THE ADMINISTRATOR GENERAL MADE LAST NIGHT ANNOUNCING THAT ELECTIONS FOR A 50-MEMBER CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY WOULD BE HELD FROM NOVEMBER 20 TO NOVEMBER 24. STEYN CLAIMED THAT THIS SHOULD NOT BE REPEAT NOT BE CONSIDERED "AS A FINAL BREAK WITH THE WESTERN INITIATIVE OR THE UN, OR AN IRREVOCABLE REJECTION OF DR. WALDHEIM'S REPORT." RATHER, HE SAID, IT SHOULD BE SEEN AS A PROCEDURE BY WHICH THE WILL OF THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH WEST AFRICAN CAN BE CLEARLY ASCERTAINED.

THE UN AND THE FIVE WESTERN COUNTRIES, HE SAID, WOULD BE INVITED TO CONSULT WITH HIM ABOUT COMING TO THE TERRITORY TO BE PRESENT DURING THE CAMPAIGN AND THE ELECTION IN ORDER TO SATISFY THEMSELVES AS TO THE FAIRNESS OF THE PROCESS.

THE AG ISSUED TWO PROCLAMATIONS (AG 63 AND 64) GIVING FORCE TO HIS DECISION. ON OCTOBER 11, A COURT OF REGISTRATION WILL CONVENE TO REGISTER PARTIES THAT WISH TO TAKE PART IN THE ELECTIONS. NO REGISTRATIONS WILL BE ACCEPTED AFTER THAT DATE. VOTING WILL TAKE PLACE FOR PARTIES NOT INDIVIDUALS AT OVER ONE THOUSAND POLLING PLACES. EACH PARTY WILL NOMINATE REPRESENTATIVES TO THE 50-MEMBER CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY PROPORTIONATE TO ITS PERCENTAGE POLL IN THE ELECTION.

COMMENT: THE AG'S RAPID SUBMISSION OF HIS DETAILED PROCLAMATIONS ON THE ELECTION SUGGEST THAT THEY HAD BEEN PREPARED WELL AHEAD OF THE SAG'S DECISION OF YESTERDAY. THE AG HAD PREVIOUSLY STATED THAT HE WAS PREPARING CONTINGENCY PLANS IN CASE THE UN PROPOSAL DID NOT PROCEED. THE LARGE NUMBER OF POLLING STATIONS, PROBABLY INCLUDING MOBILE ONES, SUGGESTS AN EXTENSIVE EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO MAKE POLLING AS CONVENIENT AS POSSIBLE. AS IN THE REGISTRATION OF VOTERS, BALLOT BOXES IN SOME AREAS WILL VERY LIKELY BE CARRIED BY VEHICLE OR HELICOPTER TO INDIVIDUAL KRAALS.

THIS WOULD BE INTENDED TO PRODUCE A RESPECTABLE AND POSSIBLY EVEN AN IMPRESSIVE TURNOUT OF VOTERS MOST OF WHOM, OUT OF APATHY OR A SENSE OF COOPERATION WITH AUTHORITY, WILL DULY CHOOSE BETWEN THE PARTIES OFFERED ON THE BALLOT. THE EFFECTIVENESS OF SWAPO AND POSSIBLY NNF EFFORTS TO ENCOURAGE A BOYCOTT OF SUCH AN ELECTION WILL DEPEND UPON THE EXTENT TO WHICH A REJECTIONIST CAMPAIGN IS PERMITTED. BUT EVEN IF SUCH A CAMPAIGN IS ALLOWED, THE GOVERNMENT'S CHANCES OF ROUNDING UP VOTERS AND ENGINEERING A MAJORITY PARTICIPATION ARE PROBABLY FAIRLY GOOD.

1978STATE242487.subject: NAMIBIA: IMPASSE ON UN TROOP SIZE

segments.text: TAKING ADVANTAGE OF A SHORT CALL ON FOURIE THIS AFTERNOON, I RAISED SUBJECT OF NAMIBIA AND SAID THAT THE PRETORIA FIVE HAD HELD A BRIEF INFORMAL MEETING THIS MORNING AT WHICH WE HAD DISCUSSED, INTER ALIA, FOREIGN MINISTER BOTHA'S REMARKS ON TV SUNDAY NIGHT HINTING THAT THE CABINET MIGHT DECIDE TO GO AHEAD WITH ELECTIONS IN NAMIBIA IF SAG DEMANDS ON THE SIZE OF THE UN MILITARY CONTINGENT WERE NOT MET. I EXPLAINED THAT WHILE NONE OF US HAD INSTRUCTIONS ON THIS SUBJECT, WE HAD AGREED THAT A CABINET DECISION TO REJECT THE WESTERN PLAN AND PROCEED WITH ELECTIONS OR EVEN SOME KIND OF REFERENDUM WOULD BE DISASTROUS.

NOTING THAT THE GERMAN AMBASSADOR HAD MENTIONED TO US THAT IN AN EARLIER CONVERSATION TODAY FOURIE HAD SAID SOMETHING TO HIM ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF A REFERENDUM TO TEST PUBLIC OPINION, I SAID THAT WE THOUGH INTERNATIONAL REACTION AGAINST AN EARLY, UNMONITORED REFERENDUM WOULD BE THE SAME AS IT WOULD BE AGAINST A SOUTH AFRICAN DECISION TO GO AHEAD ON ITS OWN WITH ELECTIONS. FOURIE TOOK THE POINT BUT MADE NO COMMENT OTHER THAN TO EXPRESS DOUBT WHETHER HE HAD USED THE WORD "REFERENDUM" IN CONTRADISTINCTION TO "ELECTIONS."

AGAIN EMPHASIZING THAT I WAS NOT SPEAKING ON INSTRUCTIONS, I STRESSED THAT THE VERY ESSENCE OF THE WESTERN PLAN WAS THE REQUIREMENT OF FREE AND FAIR ELECTIONS UNDER UN MONITORING, AND THAT NOTHING LESS COULD MEET THE REQUIREMENTS OF INTERNATIONAL ACCEPTABILITY. TO SUGGEST, AS FONMIN BOTHA REPORTEDLY DID, THAT THERE WAS A GOOD CHANCE OF WINNING RECOGNITION FOR THE RESULTS OF A PURELY INTERNAL ELECTIONS SMACKED OF SELF-DECEPTION, PARTICULARLY WHEN WE HAD COME UP WITH A PROPOSAL THAT PROVIDED ALL THE NECESSARY ELEMENTS FOR OBTAINING INTERNATIONAL ACCEPTANCE.

FOURIE SAID THAT THE ISSUE OF THE NUMBERS SEEMED INSUPERABLE. HE COULD NOT UNDERSTAND HOW THIS STAGE COULD HAVE BEEN REACHED, EMPHASIZING THAT EVEN BEFORE THE SECRETARY GENERAL'S REPORT WAS PREPARED, HE AND BOTHA HAD MADE IT VERY CLEAR TO WALDHEIM AND STEYN AND HAD MADE IT CLEAR TO AHTISAARI THAT THE QUESTION OF NUMBERS AND COMPOSITION WOULD HAVE TO BE SETTLED BEFORE THE SAG COULD AGREE TO GO AHEAD. WALDHEIM HAD SAID THEY SHOULD NOT WORRY ABOUT THIS AND AHTISAARI SAID IT WAS TOO EARLY TO DISCUSS, SO THE SAG THOUGHT THAT PERHAPS THEIR VIEWPOINT HAD BEEN UNDERSTOOD AND WOULD BE ACCOMMODATED, BUT IT WAS NOT.

FOURIE REPEATED THE VIEW THAT EVEN IF THE SIZE OF THE UN FORCE WERE ACCEPTED, THE SAG COULD HAVE NO CONFIDENCE THAT THEIR VIEWS ON COMPOSITION WOULD BE MET. THEY HAD MADE CLEAR THEY COULD NOT ACCEPT ANY COUNTRY WHICH HAD ACTIVELY SUPPORTED SWAPO BUT FELT QUITE CERTAIN THAT AT LEAST ONE SUCH COUNTRY WOULD BE CHOSEN.

SIGNIFICANTLY, WHEN I ASKED HOW THEY DEFINED "ACTIVE SUPPORT," HE USED THE EXAMPLE OF NIGERIA AS A COUNTRY WHICH HAD TAKEN A VIGOROUS PRO-SWAPO POSITION IN ITS PRONOUNCEMENTS, ADDING THAT NIGERIAN OFFICIALS (HE THOUGHT OBASANJO HIMSELF) HAD OPENLY TALKED ABOUT USING THEIR FORCES IN SUPPORT OF SWAPO AND "GOING ALL THE WAY TO CAPE TOWN IF NECESSARY." ALTHOUGH WE TALKED A BIT ABOUT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SUPPORTIVE RHETORIC AND ACTIVE SUPPORT, FOURIE APPARENTLY MEANT TO LEAVE LITTLE DOUBT THAT THE SAG COULD NOT CONSIDER NIGERIA SIFFICIENTLY IMPARTIAL TO PARTICIPATE IN TYE UNTAG MILITARY CONTINGENT.

WHEN I REFERRED TO THE PRESENT UNCERTAINTIES ABOUT THE PRIME MINISTER'S ATTITUDE TOWARD RETIREMENT OR CONTINUING AND WONDERED WHETHER THIS MADE ANY DIFFERENCE IN THE CABINET'S CONSIDERATION OF NAMIBIA, FOURIE SAID THAT AS FAR AS THE CABINET'S REJECTION OF THE FIGURE OF 7,500 WAS CONCERNED, HE DID NOT THINK IT DID MAKE ANY DIFFERENCE. HE THOUGH ALL THE MINISTERS WERE ADAMANTLY OPPOSED TO THE IDEA OF 7,500. IF VORSTER DECIDED TO STAY ON, HE SAID, THEN THE DFA HAD A PRETTY GOOD IDEA OF HIS VIEWS, BUT HE COULD NOT PREDICT WHETHER OTHERS MIGHT ACT DIFFERENTLY.

COMMENT: FOURIE REGISTERED THE POINT ABOUT ELECTIONS BUT GAVE NO INDICATION OF WHAT HE THOUGHT THE CABINET WOULD DECIDE ABOUT NAMIBIA. HE MADE IT CLEAR THAT ALL OF THE ARGUMENTS HAD BEEN PUT TO THE MINISTERS AND SEEMED RESIGNED TO THE FACT THAT THE DECISION LAY THERE. HE ALSO SEEMED AWARE THAT VERY ADVERSE CONSEQUENCES WOULD FLOW FROM REJECTION OF THE PROPOSAL BUT MADE NO APPEAL FOR MORE TIME AND GAVE NO HINT OF ANY SEARCH FOR ALTERNATIVES.
I WILL SHARE THIS MESSAGE WITH THE OTHER FOUR. EDMONDSON
WAIVER OF IMMUNITY GRANTED. CHRISTOPHER

1978STATE245918.subject: IRANIAN PERMREP TO UNITED NATIONS URGES USG ROLE IN IRANIAN CRISIS

segments.text: IN IRANIAN CRISIS

IRANIAN PERMREP TO UN FEREYDOUN HOVEYDA, BROTHER OF FORMER PRIME MINISTER, SOUGHT OUT LEONARD SEPT 25 TO URGE THAT THE USG ACT TO MAKE CLEAR TO THE SHAH THE SERIOUSNESS OF THE PRESENT SITUATION IN IRAN.

HOVEYDA, WHO STATED HE SPEAKS TO HIS BROTHER BY TELEPHONE SEVERAL TIMES A WEEK AND IMPLIED THAT THESE ARE THE VIEWS OF HIS BROTHER AS WELL AS HIS OWN, SAID THAT USG MUST DO SOMETHING TO BRING THE FACTS OF LIFE HOME TO SHAH, IN PARTICULAR A BASIC MESSAGE THAT VIGOROUS ACTION ON THE SHAH'S PART IS NECESSARY TO ESTABLISH A VISIBLE MOMENTUM WHICH WILL BE SEEN BY OTHERS AS EVIDENCE THAT THE SHAH IS IN CONTROL OF SITUATION.

A MAJOR PORTION OF HOVEYDA'S COMMENTS RELATED TO THE PROBLEM OF CHANNELS TO REACH THE SHAH. AS A FIRST POINT, HOVEYDA ASSERTED THAT USG MUST GET THROUGH TO THE SHAH A MESSAGE STATING THAT SHAH MUST GET RID OF AMB ZAHEDI. HOVEYDA SAID THAT ZAHEDI, "WITH HIS 500 WORDS OF ENGLISH," KNOWS NO ONE OF SUBSTANCE IN THE US AND CANNOT REPORT ACCURATELY ON USG VIEWS OF SITUATION IN IRAN. HOVEYDA RECOGNIZES SHAH'S DEBT TO ZAHEDI FAMILY STEMMING FROM COUP AGAINST MOSSADEGH, BUT CONSIDERS THAT DEBT SHOULD HAVE BEEN WELL PAID OFF BY NOW.

HOVEYDA STATED THAT IN TRYING TO GET MESSAGES THROUGH TO SHAH HIMSELF, DESPITE CHANNELS THROUGH HIS BROTHER AND THROUGH AN OFFICIAL ON PERSONAL STAFF OF SHAH, HE IS CONFIDENT THAT HIS MESSAGE IS DELIVERED ONLY IF HE HIMSELF PERSONALLY GOES BACK TO TEHRAN. OBVIOUSLY THERE ARE LIMITS TO THIS COURSE OF ACTION. LEONARD ASKED IF AMB SULLIVAN WAS NOT IN POSITION TO MAKE CLEAR USG VIEWS AND CONCERNS. HOVEYDA SAID THAT, AS FAR AS HE PERSONALLY KNOWS, AMB SULLIVAN HAS GOOD RELATIONS WITH THE SHAH AND IS ABLE TO EXPRESS USG CONCERNS.

REVERTING AGAIN TO INCOMPETENCE OF ZAHEDI, HOWEVER, HOVEYDA SAID THAT REPRESENTATIONS MADE BY AMB SULLIVAN TO THE SHAH CANNOT IN HIS VIEW CARRY AS MUCH FORCE AS THEY WOULD IF THEY WERE REINFORCED FROM THE IRANIAN EMBASSY IN WASHINGTON.

WITH REGARD TO SUBSTANCE, HOVEYDA SAID THAT THE BASIC MESSAGE WHICH MUST BE BROUGHT HOME TO THE SHAH IS THE NEED FOR DYNAMIC ACTION. THE SHAH SHOULD TAKE THE LEAD AND PROCLAIM AN "EMERGENCY PROGRAM OF 10 TO 15 ITEMS." IN HOVEYDA'S VIEW, IT IS NOT NECESSARY THAT THESE ALL BE APPROPRIATE ACTIONS. SOME MAY INDEED BE WRONG, BUT WHAT IS ESSENTIAL IS FOR THE SHAH TO ESTABLISH THE IMAGE THAT HE IS DOING SOMETHING AND IS IN CONTROL AND IS NOT BEING OVERWHELMED BY EVENTS.

HOVEYDA GAVE AS EXAMPLE OF SHAH'S PRESENT "IMMOBILISM" THE FACT THAT THE SHAH, INSTEAD OF PROCEEDING IMMEDIATELY TO VISIT SITE OF RECENT EARTHQUAKE, DID NOT DO SO UNTIL FOUR DAYS AFTER DISASTER, A REACTION HOVEYDA TERMED "OUTRAGEOUS."

THE IDEA OF THE SHAH BEING REPLACED BY THE CROWN PRINCE SHOULD "ABSOLUTELY BE SET ASIDE." THE SHAH HIMSELF MUST MOVE FORWARD WITH VIGOROUS ACTION TO CREATE A DEMOCRACY, TO RETRIEVE HIS PAST MISTAKES, AND TO SHOW THAT, UNDER THE SHAH'S LEADERSHIP, IRAN CAN COME INTO THE MODERN AGE. THE SHAH MUST PARTICIPATE, PLAYING THE ROLE OF THE STERN FATHER AND CRACKING DOWN ON CORRUPTION. IT WILL DO NO GOOD IF THE SHAH DOES NOT FACE UP TO THE PROBLEMS CREATED BY MEMBERS OF HIS OWN FAMILY. WHATEVER THE COST, HE MUST PUT DISTANCE BETWEEN HIMSELF AND THOSE FAMILY MEMBERS CONSIDERED TO BE CORRUPT.
IF HE DOES NOT, HE WILL NOT GAIN THE TRUST OF THE PEOPLE AND WILL BE CONSIDERED INSINCERE.

THE PRESENT PRIME MINISTER, HOVEYDA SAID, CANNOT BE AN INSTRUMENT FOR THIS. IN ALL THIS, HE SAID, IT WILL BE IMPORTANT FOR THE SHAH TO PROTITIATE AND NOT TO ANTAGONIZE RELIGIOUS ELEMENTS. THE PRIME MINISTER, WITH ONE CHILD MARRIED TO A CHRISTIAN AND ANOTHER TO A BAHAI, CANNOT POSE AS THE DEFENDER OF ORTHODOXY AND SHIA CONSERVATISM WHICH HE SUPPOSEDLY WAS SELECTED TO REPRESENT.

HOVEYDA SAID THAT HE HAD HEARD FROM A EUROPEAN COLLEAGUE OF A "CIA STUDY" CONCLUDING THAT THE SHAH MUST TAKE ACTIONS SUCH AS THESE IN ORDER TO SURVIVE. HOVEYDA SAID THAT ON HEARING THIS HE HAD MADE PARTICULAR EFFORTS TO GET THE GIST OF IT TO THE SHAH. KNOWING THAT THE IRANIAN EMBASSY IN WASHINGTON WOULD NOT REPORT THIS, HE HAD DONE SO HIMSELF. WHAT IS NOW IMPORTANT. HOVEYDA STATED, IS FOR THE USG TO STATE THIS CONCLUSION TO THE SHAH DIRECTLY, NOT OBLIQUELY AND NOT ONLY THROUGH EMBASSY TEHRAN.
HOVEYDA, URGING THAT EVERY POSSIBLE CHANNEL BE USED, ASKED IF IT WOULD BE POSSIBLE TO SEND A PERSONAL ENVOY TO MAKE THE MESSAGE ABSOLUTELY CLEAR.

HOVEYDA RAISED ALSO THE POSSIBILITY OF A US APPROACH TO THE SOVIETS REGARDING OUR MUTUAL INTEREST IN A STABLE IRAN. HE STATED THAT HE "KNOWS" THAT THE USG IS NOT BEHIND THE PRESENT TURMOIL IN IRAN. HE BELIEVES THAT THE USSR IS NOT, EITHER. HE STATED THAT VICTOR LESSIOVSKI, "THE SENIOR KGB AGENT AT THE UN," HAD RECENTLY APPROACHED HIM TO ASSURE HIM THAT THE SOVIET UNION WAS NOT BEHIND THE RECENT TROUBLES. HOVEYDA BELIEVES LESSIOVSKI.

HOVEYDA SAYS HE KNOWS THAT THE SOVIET UNION WISHES TO TAKE OVER IRAN ONE DAY, BUT HE DOES NOT THINK THE SOVIETS ARE PREPARED TO MOVE NOW SINCE THEY DO NOT TRUST THE IRANIAN COMMUNIST PARTY. RECOGNIZING THE PROBLEMS INVOLVED, HOVEYDA NONETHELESS EXPRESSED THE HOPE THAT THE USG MIGHT BE ABLE TO DISCUSS THE MATTER WITH THE SOVIETS WITH A VIEW TO ASSURING THE SHAH THAT NEITHER COUNTRY SOUGHT HIS FALL FROM POWER. YOUNG
SUMMARY: DEPARTMENT HAS RECEIVED REPORTS FROM VARIOUS U.S. (AND JAPANESE) COMPANIES DURING PAST THREE DAYS CONCERNING: A) IGAT PIPELINE EXPLOSION ON SEPTEMBER 21

REPORTED GENERAL STRIKE OF DAILY RATE EMPLOYEES AT MAJOR OIL PRODUCTION AND LOADING FACILITIES; AND C) IMMINENT DISPLACEMENT OF NIOC DIRECTOR HUSHANG ANSARY. EMBASSY REACTION/ COMMENTS ON THESE REPORTS WOULD BE APPRECIATED. END SUMMARY.

IGAT PIPELINE EXPLOSION. ACCORDING TO JAPANESE AND U.S. COMPANY OFFICIALS, REPORTED EXPLOSION OCCURRED ON THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 21, AT POINT IN PIPELINE ROUTE APPROXIMATELY 17 MILES SOUTH OF QUM. BLAST REPORTEDLY DESTROYED 500 FOOT-SECTION OF LARGE DIAMETER PIPELINE. NO CASUALTIES MENTIONED. PRESS ITEM QUOTED UNNAMED NIGC SPOKESMAN AS BLAMING TERRORISTS FOR THE INCIDENT.

DAILY RATE WORKER STRIKE. ACCORDING TO EXECUTIVE OF U.S. FIRM WHICH BELONGS TO CONSORTIUM, GENERAL WALK-OUT OF DAILY RATE EMPLOYEES (DRE'S), MOSTLY IRANIAN, TOOK PLACE ON MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 25, AND INVOLVED ALL MAJOR KHUZESTAN PRODUCTION FACILITIES AS WELL AS KHARG ISLAND LOADING TERMINAL. STRIKE BEGAN WITH ABOUT 50 TO 60 PERCENT OF DRE'S PARTICIPATING AND REACHED 100 PERCENT LEVEL BY FOLLOWING DAY, ACCORDING TO COMPANY'S TEHRAN REP. REPRESENTATIVES OF MINISTRY OF LABOR, SYNDICATES, DRE'S, OSCO AND NIOC CONVENED SPECIAL MEETING SEPTEMBER 26 TO DISCUSS SITUATION. DRE SPOKESMEN PRESENTED COMPANY WITH LIST OF 48 UNOFFICIAL DEMANDS, TOPPED BY REQUEST FOR 50 PERCENT WAGE INCREASE.
AS FAR AS WE KNOW, ALLEGED GRIEVANCES CONSIST ONLY OF ECONOMIC DEMANDS; THERE ARE APPARENTLY NO POLITICAL ISSUES.

THUS FAR, EFFECT ON OPERATIONS HAS BEEN MINIMAL. PRODUCTION IS OFF ABOUT 190,000 B/D CAUSED BY SHUT-DOWN OF TWO SMALLER FIELDS. ACCORDING TO COMPANY SOURCE, PROBLEM COULD DEVELOP AT KHARG TERMINAL WHERE DRES' SERVICES ARE NECESSARY FOR BERTHING OF TANKERS. OSCO IS ATTEMPTING TO LINE UP CONTRACT TUGS TO ALLEVIATE PROBLEM. IRANIAN NAVY HAS REPORTEDLY PUT PERSONNEL AT DISPOSAL OF OSCO AND NIOC TO HELP OPERATE KHARG. COMPANY SOURCE OPINED THAT IF STRIKE EXTENDS BEYOND 3 DAYS OR SO, PROBLEMS WILL BECOME MUCH MORE ACUTE.

HUSHANG ANSARY. U.S. BANKER WHO PARTICIPATED IN DISCUSSION WITH GOI DELEGATION TO WORLD BANK MEETINGS CAME AWAY WITH DEFINITE MESSAGE THAT ANSARY'S DISMISSAL WAS IMMINENT. ACCORDING TO THIS OFFICIAL, ANSARY HAS BEEN TARRED WITH THE BRUSHES OF CORRUPTION AND BAHAI CONNECTIONS (WORD IS THAT ANSARY'S FATHER WAS BAHAI). OIL COMPANY OFFICIAL CITED IN PARAS THREE AND FOUR MENTIONED HE HAD HEARD SAME RUMORS ABOUT ANSARY. LATTER SOURCE FELT THIS WAS REASON FOR "DRIFT" AT NIOC AND POSSIBLY EXPLAINED WHY MATTERS HAD GOTTEN OUT OF HAND ON THE STRIKE.

WE PASS THESE REPORTS ON FOR YOUR POSSIBLE COMMENT AND CLARIFICATION. AS YOU CAN IMAGINE, BOARDROOM IMPRESSIONS ABOUT IRAN ARE BEING SHAPED BY THIS KIND OF INFORMATION AND ANYTHING YOU CAN GIVE US TO SET RECORD STRAIGHT WILL BE APPRECIATED. CHRISTOPHER
